Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

10.1126/sciadv.aec9550.title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
10.1126/sciadv.aec9550.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

10.1126/sciadv.aee5373.title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
10.1126/sciadv.aee5373.abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission-driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

10.1126/sciadv.aef3522.title: SPRIZ (CCDC127) protein conserved in deuterostome animals is a rigid OMM-IMM tether that locally sets mitochondrial IMS volume
10.1126/sciadv.aef3522.abstract: The double-membrane nature of mitochondria generates an intermembrane volume through which ions, reactive oxygen species, and metabolites must flux to reach the matrix or cytosol, but whether this volume is a genetically specified structure remains unknown. We identify SPRIZ (spatial regulator of the intermembrane zone), the product of Ccdc127 , a gene conserved across deuterostome animals. SPRIZ assembles into an ∼18-nanometer homodimeric tether anchored in the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) and inserted into the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) through vertebrate-specific hydrophobic loops, physically spacing the two membranes and setting local intermembrane volume. Cryo-electron tomography of native mitochondria revealed rod-like densities spanning the intermembrane space (IMS), consistent with SPRIZ’s predicted rigid coiled-coil architecture and membrane-spanning topology. In mouse liver, two-dimensional morphometry measured ∼3-fold expansion of IMS area with SPRIZ and ∼5.5-fold with lengthened mitochondrial artificial increaser of the IMS (MARTINI); 3D electron tomography confirmed MARTINI’s greater OMM-IMM separation and normalized IMS volume. This expansion was functionally validated by increased 14 C-mannitol accessibility to the IMS and by impaired mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake. Constitutive Ccdc127/SPRIZ knockout produced viable mice and, in liver mitochondria, preserved overall ultrastructure but caused modest IMS expansion, consistent with loss of local OMM-IMM constraints that stabilize membrane geometry at discrete sites. We therefore identify IMS volume as a genetically encoded and tunable architectural parameter of vertebrate mitochondria. In this model, SPRIZ is a molecular spacing system that locally sets OMM-IMM separation, shaping the environment through which metabolites, ions, and signals diffuse and establishing local gradients within the IMS.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh1580.title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
10.1126/sciadv.aeh1580.abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. A single week of contact, and in some cases as few as 3 days, provides sufficient symbionts to initiate sustained and full self-recovery. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. However, symbiont transfer via polyp uptake occurs immediately upon contact in both same-genet and mixed-genet pairings, revealing an additional, slower pathway for symbiont transfer that is insufficient on its own to support colony recovery. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized natural process for efficiently reintroducing symbionts to bleached corals, providing a foundation for research into potential recovery interventions.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh8222.title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
10.1126/sciadv.aeh8222.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children. K. pneumoniae isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from K. pneumoniae neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative K. pneumoniae vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of K. pneumoniae. Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal K. pneumoniae infection.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh9563.title: Vitamin D binding protein in ventral CA3 of the hippocampus drives stress-induced depression
10.1126/sciadv.aeh9563.abstract: The ventral hippocampus plays a crucial role in regulating emotional and motivated behaviors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. Here, we identified elevated expression of vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) in the hippocampi of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-susceptible mice, which correlated with the severity of depression-like behaviors. Notably, VDBP up-regulation was specifically in ventral CA3 excitatory (vCA3 CaMKIIα ) neurons. CA3 CaMKIIα VDBP overexpression led to inhibited neuronal activity, synaptic and dendritic impairments, and, ultimately, depression-like behaviors. Conversely, vCA3 CaMKIIα -specific VDBP knockdown enhanced resilience to chronic stress. Mechanistically, VDBP directly interacted with PIK3R3 to inhibit the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway in a cell-autonomous manner, leading to excessive autophagy and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. Chemogenetic activation, intervention using the Akt-specific activator SC79, and site-specific mutation disrupting the VDBP-PIK3R3 interaction ameliorated vCA3 CaMKIIα VDBP-induced depression-like phenotypes. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical involvement of vCA3 CaMKIIα neuron-derived VDBP in stress-induced depressive pathology and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for MDD.

10.1126/sciadv.aei1213.title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
10.1126/sciadv.aei1213.abstract: The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently, tic mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress-responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day-dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in tic mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress-responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

10.1126/sciadv.aei9275.title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO 2 release in alpine landscapes
10.1126/sciadv.aei9275.abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering-driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

10.1126/sciadv.aed6878.title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
10.1126/sciadv.aed6878.abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

10.1126/sciadv.aee5884.title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
10.1126/sciadv.aee5884.abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh0802.title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
10.1126/sciadv.aeh0802.abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

10.1126/sciadv.aei0002.title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
10.1126/sciadv.aei0002.abstract: Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C −1 between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

10.1126/sciadv.aei2144.title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
10.1126/sciadv.aei2144.abstract: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and • OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film • OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase • OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

10.1126/sciadv.ady6737.title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
10.1126/sciadv.ady6737.abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

10.1126/sciadv.aea9749.title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
10.1126/sciadv.aea9749.abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. On average, 916 million people per year were exposed to at least one coexposure day, increasing by 287 million people per decade. The global annual average exposed days per person was 1.3 days, rising from 1.0 days in 2000-2009 to 1.7 days in 2010-2019. Coexposure person-days increased by 5.5 billion per decade, of which 70.5% was attributable to increasing coexposure intensity and 29.5% to population growth. Countries with a low human development index (HDI) experienced the highest coexposure days per person and the greatest increases. These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

10.1126/sciadv.aed2474.title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
10.1126/sciadv.aed2474.abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

10.1126/sciadv.aed7447.title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
10.1126/sciadv.aed7447.abstract: Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ L , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing-based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ L to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ L to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ L to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

10.1126/sciadv.aee5162.title: The network structure of the urban revolution
10.1126/sciadv.aee5162.abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world-like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg5408.title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
10.1126/sciadv.aeg5408.abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh4671.title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
10.1126/sciadv.aeh4671.abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3059.title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3059.abstract: Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant-derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black-coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m −2 ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m −2 from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh0707.title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
10.1126/sciadv.aeh0707.abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

10.1126/sciadv.aef0605.title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
10.1126/sciadv.aef0605.abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh5001.title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
10.1126/sciadv.aeh5001.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

10.1126/sciadv.aei9401.title: Remote allosteric control of single-atom Cu sites in Zr-MOFs enables selective CH 4 hydroxylation
10.1126/sciadv.aei9401.abstract: Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu 1 to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO 2 , -H, and -CH 3 ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu 1 sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu 1 sites, thereby facilitating CH 4 activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO 2 -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu 1 - • OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu 1 /U6-NO 2 achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h −1 with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

10.1126/sciadv.aec7686.title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
10.1126/sciadv.aec7686.abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification-based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning-assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

10.1126/sciadv.aef5666.title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red-sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
10.1126/sciadv.aef5666.abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red-sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

10.1126/sciadv.aem6116.title: Rewilding the atoll engine
10.1126/sciadv.aem6116.abstract: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience.

10.1126/sciadv.aem6534.title: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the enduring value of old ideas
10.1126/sciadv.aem6534.abstract: Alaska’s Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ looks a lot like fluted point sites south of the North American ice sheets. Archaeologists have expected this for 60 years.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh0904.title: All-optical control of nonlinear emission from resonant metasurfaces
10.1126/sciadv.aeh0904.abstract: Nonlinear optics underpins a broad range of photonic technologies, from classical and quantum light sources to emerging nonlinear photonic neural networks. Yet, conventional nonlinear-optical devices exhibit static functionality: Their transfer characteristics and emission profiles are dictated by the intrinsic nonlinear process and locked by fabrication, limiting adaptability. Here, we introduce an ultrathin metasurface platform that enables dynamic reconfiguration of nonlinear functionality in a contactless fashion. By leveraging all-optical control of the optical torque exerted on liquid crystal molecules infiltrating a resonant metasurface, we achieve tunable polynomial nonlinear transfer functions based on the third-harmonic generation process. This mechanism further allows reconfigurable modulation of nonlinear weighting across different diffraction orders, revealing a previously unexplored interplay between mode structure and nonlinear emission. Our approach opens up a pathway toward field-programmable nonlinear photonic systems, offering unprecedented flexibility for reconfigurable nonlinear signal processing and adaptive photonic computing.

10.1126/sciadv.aeb0624.title: Bioinspired architected catalyst for efficient water purification: Bridging reactivity, reusability, and catalytic component utilization
10.1126/sciadv.aeb0624.abstract: Achieving highly efficient water purification remains a formidable challenge due to intricate coupling among catalytic efficiency, mechanical robustness, and mass transport. Here, we create a bioinspired architected catalyst featuring microscale shell-based frameworks with atomically dispersed Mn-N 4 sites, fabricated by digital light processing and ultrasonic decoration. Their synergy-where the starfish- and bone-inspired architecture minimizes stress concentration for reusability and enhances pollutant-site contact for mass transport, while the Mn-N 4 sites facilitate •OH-mediated oxidation-collectively amplifies overall performance beyond the contributions of either component alone. Compared with conventional pellet catalysts, the architected catalyst exhibits a 22.1-fold increase in strength and a 4.56-fold increase in normalized reaction kinetics, resulting in more than 95% degradation with 0.08% active component consumption. It occupies the previously unattained region in the catalytic efficiency ( K value) versus metal utilization (active component content) diagram of reported powder and supported catalysts. This work demonstrates a generalizable strategy for designing catalysts that unite reactivity, reusability, and catalytic component utilization.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh5460.title: Regulating phonon-carrier transport by interfacial symmetry breaking in thermoelectric multilayers
10.1126/sciadv.aeh5460.abstract: More than half of global primary energy is dissipated as low-grade waste heat, yet thermoelectric conversion remains constrained by the intrinsic coupling between phonon and charge transport. Here, we introduce graded interfacial size distribution as a thermodynamic design variable that breaks translational symmetry in multilayers, enabling anisotropic regulation of phonon-carrier transport. Using bismuth telluride (Bi 2 Te 3 )/metal [gold, silver, and platinum (Pt)] multilayers as a model system, we demonstrate that multiscale interface distributions induce broadband phonon suppression through the coexistence of interfacial scattering, coherent interference, and localization. This yields an ultralow cross-plane thermal conductivity of 0.22 watts per meter per kelvin and a high room-temperature ZT of 1.51 in Bi 2 Te 3 /Pt films. Concurrently, asymmetric metal-semiconductor interfaces create quasi-two-dimensional accumulation channels that enhance in-plane carrier mobility while preserving energy filtering, delivering a power factor of 176.2 microwatts per centimeter per square kelvin at 300 kelvin. The graded architecture enables high performance in both vertical and flexible planar devices, illustrating a general strategy in which interface distribution, not merely composition, governs anisotropic heat-charge transport. Our findings establish statistical interface engineering as a platform for thermoelectric energy harvesting and solid-state cooling.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg3475.title: KRAS is required for plexiform neurofibroma formation and represents a targetable vulnerability in established tumors
10.1126/sciadv.aeg3475.abstract: Patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 develop Schwann cell tumors called neurofibromas that arise within peripheral nerves, driven by loss of neurofibromin and consequent increased RAS/RAF/MEK signaling. MEK inhibitors achieve partial responses for benign neurofibromas but are limited by toxicity and incomplete efficacy, necessitating alternative approaches. Using the Dhh- Cre; Nf1 fl/fl neurofibroma mouse model, we found that genetic ablation of Kras , but not Hras , markedly reduced neurofibroma development, inhibited MAPK activation, and rescued disrupted Remak bundles that are a morphologic hallmark of neurofibromas. These findings reveal a RAS paralog-specific requirement for KRAS in NF1-deficient neurofibroma initiation. Pharmacological KRAS inhibition with BI6674, an orally bioavailable KRAS multi inhibitor, reduced tumor volume and proliferation in established neurofibromas and remodeled the tumor immune microenvironment, decreasing macrophages and dendritic cells. Combining KRAS and MEK inhibition further enhanced tumor regression. These findings demonstrate that KRAS is essential for neurofibroma formation and represents a promising therapeutic target, supporting clinical evaluation of KRAS inhibition for neurofibromas in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh7029.title: A built-in brake for plant immunity: Resistance (R) protein-mediated immunity is fine-tuned by R gene analogs
10.1126/sciadv.aeh7029.abstract: Potato late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans threatens global food security. Unlike the fact that most race-specific resistance to P. infestans ( Rpi ) genes is rapidly overcome by evolving pathogen populations, the R8 gene from Solanum demissum has conferred durable, quantitative resistance for nearly a century despite encoding a canonical coiled-coil-type nucleotide-binding, leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein. We identified specific R8 gene analogs that act as negative modulators of R8 -mediated immunity. These R8 gene analogs lack independent resistance functions but perturb the recognition of avirulence effector Avr8 by R8 and interfere with oligomerization and plasma membrane association of NRC2, a helper NLR essential for the R8 signaling pathway. Stable overexpression of such RGAs effectively compromises R8 -mediated resistance in both potato and Nicotiana benthamiana . We propose that this endogenous regulation balances the intensity of R8 -mediated immunity, likely reducing selection pressure on the pathogen population and prolonging resistance durability. Our findings reveal a regulatory layer where genetically linked RGAs control resistance (R) protein-mediated immunity, providing a conceptual framework for durable resistance breeding.

10.1126/sciadv.aef7481.title: Triggering charge redistribution-induced oxygen spillover mechanism in VO x -supported IrSn alloy toward industrial water electrolysis
10.1126/sciadv.aef7481.abstract: Developing advanced iridium (Ir)-based oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Unfortunately, conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) pathways suffer from an activity-stability trade-off, posing substantial challenges for catalyst design. Here, we report a charge-redistribution-induced oxygen (O) spillover strategy by designing amorphous VO x -supported iridium-tin (IrSn) alloy OER catalysts, which can effectively transfer the poisoning oxygenated intermediates and maintain Ir valence stability (+2.5) during the dynamic OER to enhance activity and stability. In particular, the IrSn-VO x -based PEMWE anode can deliver a current density of 3.0 amperes per square centimeter @ 1.798 volts (0.4 milligrams of platinum and Ir per square centimeter), surpassing the US Department of Energy (DOE) 2026 targets. A 25-square centimeter PEMWE operates stably for 5000 hours at industrial currents (≥25 amperes) with an exceptionally low degradation rate of 5.6 microvolts per hour, representing one of the best OER catalysts reported for practical PEMWEs. Theoretical calculations predict that the charge redistribution within IrSn-VO x could reduce the kinetic energy barrier for *O spillover (from Ir to VO x ) by 69% relative to O-O coupling, thus triggering the O spillover against the Ir overoxidation/dissolution. Consequently, IrSn-VO x follows a support-involved LOM pathway with a reduced rate-determining-step barrier (0.37 electron volts) relative to IrSn following AEM (0.66 electron volts). In addition, Sn doping in IrSn-VO x can further promote the regeneration of VO x lattice O and improve stability.

10.1126/sciadv.aef4627.title: Starch granules are instructive scaffolds for synergistic reinforcement and dissipation in hydrogel composites
10.1126/sciadv.aef4627.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft material design is the competition between rigidity and dynamicity, as stiffening mechanisms typically suppress energy dissipation. Here, we demonstrate that starch granules serve as instructive scaffolds that overcome this constraint, enabling the synergistic amplification of both elastic reinforcement and dynamic dissipation in hydrogels. We show that engineering the charge and structure of the filler-matrix interface enhances this synergistic response, which we propose arises from a dual-action physical mechanism: Filler-induced polymer bundling of the polymer matrix provides structural reinforcement, while transient filler-matrix hydrogen bonding facilitates dissipation. Moreover, we reveal that binary blends of disparate filler species unexpectedly suppress these emergent properties, which we argue arises from enhanced entropic mixing. Our results provide a physical framework to overcome current design limitations in soft composites and sculpt their viscoelastic response from synergistic enhancement to strategic suppression for applications ranging from high-performance soft robotics to biomimetic tissue engineering.

10.1126/sciadv.aej5359.title: A transient RNP compartment boosts translation and growth of mammalian oocytes
10.1126/sciadv.aej5359.abstract: Mammalian oocytes undergo an extended growth phase, during which transcription gradually declines. To sustain meiotic divisions and early embryonic development, growing oocytes must accumulate maternal stores and tightly regulate translation. Using immunofluorescence, mass spectrometry, electron microscopy, RNA sequencing, and live ex vivo ovarian tissue-slice imaging, we identified a transient ribonucleoprotein-organelle compartment in growing mouse oocytes, which we named the Zollo body. Although it resembles the Balbiani body observed in nongrowing oocytes of many vertebrate species, the Zollo body arises during growth and shows nascent translation and phospho-mTOR enrichment. Pharmacological dissolution of the Zollo body arrests follicle and oocyte growth in cultured ovarian tissue slices. Thus, the Zollo body is a transient, translation-associated compartment required for normal follicle and oocyte growth.

10.1126/sciadv.aef8133.title: Orthogonal DNA barcoding enables subpopulation-resolved extracellular vesicle miRNA profiling
10.1126/sciadv.aef8133.abstract: Extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs (EV-miRNAs) hold promise for liquid biopsy, but their clinical utility is hindered by EV heterogeneity. Here, we report DEEPER, a DNA-encoded orthogonal recognition platform for selective barcoding of tumor-derived EV subpopulations and in situ miRNA profiling. DEEPER uses four aptamers targeting Cluster of Differentiation 44 (CD44), Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor‌ (EGFR), Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2‌ (HER2), and ‌Programmed Death-Ligand 1(PD-L1) to generate orthogonal barcodes that distinguish 15 EV subpopulations. Barcoded EVs then undergo targeted membrane fusion with liposome probes, enabling sensitive in situ analysis of subpopulation-specific miRNAs. In a 60-sample cohort of patients with gastric cancer (GC) and healthy donors (HDs), DEEPER identified a high-performing signature, GC-EV miRNA Prime, comprising EGFR + , EGFR + HER2 + , and EGFR + HER2 + CD44 + EVs, which achieved 98.3% diagnostic accuracy. The same profiling framework also assessed tumor invasiveness with 95.5% accuracy. Mechanistic studies further showed that these EV-miRNAs contribute to tumor progression. In summary, DEEPER not only confirmed the clinical application value of EV-miRNA-based liquid biopsy but also provided unique insights through the EV subpopulations into the mechanisms driving cancer development.

10.1126/sciadv.aee5269.title: Extremely low thermal conductivity in rigid layered hybrid perovskites
10.1126/sciadv.aee5269.abstract: Materials with exceptionally low thermal conductivity are desirable for thermal insulation and waste heat recovery. While foams and aerogels boast ultralow thermal conductivities akin to air, lack of mechanical stiffness in these soft materials necessitates a paradigm shift in materials design that can offer thermal insulation and mechanical rigidity simultaneously. Here, we show that spun-cast layered hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite thin films, azobenzene ethyl ammonium lead iodides, exhibit a record-low thermal conductivity, down to ∼0.04 watts per meter per kelvin at room temperature, while maintaining mechanical rigidity with an elastic modulus of 7.7 gigapascals that surpasses that of most plastics, foams, and aerogels. This unusual combination of ultralow thermal conductivity and high mechanical rigidity is attributed to the specially engineered organic cations in the layered structure. Our finding highlights the potential of molecular engineering in hybrid layered structures to push the extreme of thermal insulation in dense, rigid solids.

10.1126/sciadv.aef7696.title: Ribosomal protein bL27 protects translating ribosomes from tmRNA-SmpB
10.1126/sciadv.aef7696.abstract: Bacterial ribosomal protein bL27 is universally conserved, and its amino terminus is adjacent to the peptidyl transfer center, yet its roles in translation remain unclear. Combining genetics, biochemistry, and molecular dynamics, we show that bL27 has an unexpected role in preventing transfer-messenger RNA (tmRNA)-small protein B (SmpB), molecules involved in the trans-translation bacterial ribosome rescue mechanism, from interfering with protein synthesis. Deletion of the bL27 gene causes a 10,000-fold decrease in viability, and this defect is partially rescued by deletion of the gene encoding tmRNA. Addition of tmRNA-SmpB to in vitro translation reactions decreases the rate of protein synthesis by ribosomes lacking bL27 but has no effect on wild-type ribosomes. Molecular dynamics simulations also indicate that bL27 can slow the movement of tmRNA on the ribosome. These data link trans-translation and bL27 and support a model in which the amino terminus of bL27 acts as a gatekeeper to prevent tmRNA from sterically interfering with tRNA (transfer RNA) on the ribosome.

10.1126/sciadv.aec2917.title: Observation of mirror-odd and mirror-even spin texture in ultrathin epitaxially strained RuO 2 films
10.1126/sciadv.aec2917.abstract: Recently, rutile ruthenium dioxide (RuO 2 ) has attracted renewed interest due to expectations of prominent altermagnetic spin splitting. However, accumulating experimental evidence suggests that, in its bulk and thick-film forms, RuO 2 does not display any form of magnetic ordering. Despite this, the spin structure of RuO 2 remains largely unexplored in the ultrathin limit, where substrate-imposed epitaxial strain can be substantial. Here, we use spin-resolved angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, supported by ab initio calculations, to reveal the electronic structure of 2-nanometer-thick epitaxial RuO 2 heterostructures. We observe an unconventional spin texture characterized by the coexistence of mirror-even and mirror-odd momentum-dependent components. A comprehensive symmetry analysis rules out nonmagnetic origins of this spin texture. These findings suggest an emergent nonrelativistic spin structure enabled by epitaxial strain in the ultrathin limit, marking a distinct departure from the behavior of relaxed or bulk RuO 2 . Our work opens previously unexplored perspectives for exploring symmetry-breaking mechanisms and spin textures in oxide heterostructures.

10.1002/adma.75347.title: A 3D-Printed Biochemical-Mechano-Thermally Responsive Multicellular Tumor Organoid Platform Decodes Biochemical-Physical Regulation of Cancer-Immune Crosstalk and Chemoresistance
10.1002/adma.75347.abstract: ABSTRACT Oral tumors are not shaped by biochemical signals alone; they also evolve within mechanically active and thermally fluctuating microenvironments that critically regulate malignant progression, immune remodeling, and therapeutic resistance. Here, we develop a dynamic bioorthogonal organoid platform that couples a 3D-printed photothermal elastic scaffold with an interpenetrating hydrogel network derived from decellularized oral mucosa extracellular matrix, enabling the reconstruction of in vivo-like structural support, matrix-derived biochemical cues, spatial cellular compartmentalization, and dynamic physical stimulation. Through click chemistry-mediated cell anchorage and hydrogel encapsulation, oral cancer cells and macrophages are spatially organized into a compartmentalized cancer-immune niche. Under cyclic mechanical stretch and near-infrared-triggered periodic photothermal stimulation, dynamic culture markedly enhances cancer cell proliferation and glycolytic reprogramming while concomitantly polarizing macrophages toward a pro-tumoral M2 phenotype. In both monoculture and coculture settings, biochemical-mechano-thermal stimulation substantially increases cancer cell chemoresistance. Mechanistically, these biochemical-physical cues activate stress-adaptive and survival programs while enriching cancer stem-like populations. In a xenograft mouse model exposed to in vivo biochemical, mechanical and thermal stimulation, dynamic conditioning markedly accelerates tumor progression, enhances metastatic potential, and confers pronounced chemoresistance. Together, this study establishes a biomimetic multicellular tumor platform for uncovering how dynamic biochemical-physical cues orchestrate cancer-immune crosstalk and therapeutic failure.

10.1002/adma.75370.title: Asymmetric-Isomerization Dimer Acceptors via Modular Molecular Design Enable Highly Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75370.abstract: ABSTRACT Dimer acceptors are attractive for organic solar cells (OSCs) owing to their combination of stability and high efficiency, yet the efficiency of dimer-based binary devices has long stagnated below 20%. The limitation stems from weak intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and poor locally excited/charge-transfer (LE/CT) state hybridization, which are direct consequences of the canceled dipole moments in symmetric dimer architectures. In this work, we adopt an asymmetric-isomerization strategy to design two novel dual-asymmetric isomeric dimer acceptors QCl-YF and QF-YCl. Compared with QCl-YF, QF-YCl exhibits an enhanced ICT effect as evidenced by a larger electron-hole spatial separation, which promotes LE/CT hybridization and enables more efficient carrier dynamics. Moreover, the stronger electrostatic potential and dipole moment of QF-YCl enhances the intermolecular interactions to improve donor/acceptor compatibility and film-forming process in blend film, consequently leading to more ordered film morphology. Consequently, the QF-YCl-based device achieves a record PCE of 20.23% (vs. 19.60% for QCl-YF), achieving the highest efficiency for dimer-based binary OSCs. This work demonstrates that asymmetric-isomerization is a precise and effective design strategy for high-performance dimer acceptors.

10.1002/adma.75300.title: Pre-Intercalated Cation Optimizing Proton Topochemistry for High-Performance Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75300.abstract: ABSTRACT Cation pre-intercalated oxides have been widely explored as cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Although the influence of intercalants on the material structure and Zn 2+ storage capacity has been adequately studied, an in-depth understanding of the influence of intercalants on proton storage is still lacking. Especially, proton transport exhibits ultrafast kinetics as an ideal charge carrier, playing a crucial role in the performance of AZIBs. We show that pre-intercalated K + in K 0.5 V 6 O 13 (KVO) not only reinforces the [VO] framework but also optimizes the hydrogen-bonded network composed of confined lattice water, achieving ultrafast proton transport. Benefiting from the optimization of proton topochemistry, the capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability of KVO improve significantly. KVO delivers a high reversible capacity of 462.9 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 and 82.3% retention after 20000 cycles at 20 A g −1 . Even with the high mass loading of 19.2 mg cm −2 , a KVO||Zn pouch cell with 539.2 mAh capacity can achieve stable cycling for more than 300 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . This work provides new insights into how pre-intercalated cations affect the proton topochemistry and electrochemical performance of inorganic cathodes.

10.1002/adma.75355.title: A Quasi-n-i-p Architecture Realized by Sequential Lamination Delivers 20.58% Efficiency in Inverted Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75355.abstract: ABSTRACT Inverted organic solar cells (OSCs) are promising for their enhanced operational stability; however, their power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) have lagged those of conventional devices, largely due to interfacial losses at the active layer/metal-oxide interface. Here, we develop a sequential lamination strategy to construct a quasi-n-i-p active layer comprising an acceptor-rich layer, a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) core, and a donor-rich layer. This vertically engineered architecture establishes cascade energy-level alignment and preserves interfacial integrity, thereby facilitating efficient charge extraction and suppressing recombination losses. As a result, the optimal device achieves a PCE of 20.58%, with a certified efficiency of 20.07%, placing it among the highest reported for single-junction inverted OSCs. This architecture was successfully fabricated with different donor-rich layers, BHJ cores, and acceptor-rich layers, demonstrating broader material applicability across multiple material combinations. Interfacial adhesion and vertical compositional control improve electrical continuity, enhance charge generation and transport, and reduce trap-assisted and bimolecular recombination, leading to higher open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current density, and fill factor. This work provides a scalable route to active-layer engineering in inverted OSCs and offers a general strategy for high-performance organic photovoltaic fabrication.

10.1002/adma.75361.title: Strain-Controlled Pt Single-Atom Catalysts on Crumpled MXene Supports for Highly Active Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adma.75361.abstract: ABSTRACT Strain engineering offers a powerful means to regulate the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of active metal sites, yet a general framework linking strain to electrocatalytic performance remains elusive beyond the conventional d-band model. Here we report crumpled double-transition-metal MXene nanosheets (Mo 2 TiC 2 T x ) decorated with Pt single atoms, in which a tunable strain field is introduced through a physical diaphragm balloon method. The resulting cMo 2 TiC 2 T x -Pt SA catalyst exhibits outstanding alkaline hydrogen evolution performance, requiring overpotentials of only 24.9 and 75.5 mV to reach 10 and 50 mA cm −2 , respectively, together with a mass activity of 11 859 mA mgPt −1 , around 178-fold higher than commercial Pt/C, a Tafel slope of 31.61 mV dec −1 and excellent durability. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that the ordered long-range strain field around isolated Pt sites accelerates interfacial water activation while preserving near-optimal H adsorption, thereby facilitating H 2 release. The resulting catalyst delivered a high current density of 3 A cm −2 at a low voltage of 1.98 V and maintained stable operation at 1000 mA cm −2 for over 500 h. These performance metrics underscore the potential of cMo 2 TiC 2 T x -Pt SA for industrial applications.

10.1002/adma.75260.title: Unlocking the Interfacial Activity of Insoluble Lithium Salts for Stable Lithium Batteries
10.1002/adma.75260.abstract: ABSTRACT Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge-transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high-lattice-energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis-acidic Li + sites directly onto an aramid-scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution-diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li + solvation and enhanced anion-derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6 Li/ 7 Li isotope tracing identify Li 2 SO 4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP-LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP-LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO 4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll-to-roll manufacturing across diverse Ah-level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m −2 . This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next-generation high-energy-density batteries.

10.1002/adma.75237.title: Time-Resolved Physically Unclonable Functions Enabled by Solvent-Free Scalable Boron-Based Ultralong Phosphorescent Systems for Machine-Learning-Resilient Optical Encryption
10.1002/adma.75237.abstract: ABSTRACT Anti-counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time-resolved physically unclonable function (TR-PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high-dimensional temporal encoding. Central to this approach, boron-based room-temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials are developed via covalent coupling with coumarin derivatives using a solvent-free strategy that is readily scalable to kilogram-level production, exhibiting a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of over 2 s, an ultralong afterglow visible for up to 30 s, and color-tunable emission. The formation of rigid B-O-C linkages spatially isolates emissive centers, suppressing energy transfer and preserving temporally independent decay channels-an essential prerequisite for high-entropy time-resolved encoding. Randomly embedding these multi-emissive RTP units into a polymer matrix forms a complex encryption structure that enables a dual-entropy encoding mechanism with both spectral and temporal dimensions, generating dynamic time keys for authentication. Moreover, we propose a matched time-gated authentication framework that achieves >99% identification accuracy within 1.2 s while exhibiting resistance against the tested generative machine-learning attacks. This work proposes a practical materials platform and a time-gated authentication strategy, offering a scalable technological path for the development of dynamic optical encryption tags.

10.1002/adma.75320.title: Dual-Encrypted Ultraviolet Optical Communication Driven by Opto-Piezoelectric Coupling in Two-Dimensional Flexible Ferroelectric Single-Crystalline Thin-Films
10.1002/adma.75320.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high-security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual-wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software-based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware-level security. Herein, we report a dual-encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system based on BA 2 EA 2 Pb 3 Br 10 ( 1 , where BA is n-butylamine and EA is ethylamine) ferroelectric single-crystalline thin-films (SCFs). The 1 ferroelectric SCFs show a photoresponsivity that reaches 230% of the original level under +1.13% tensile strain. Notably, we innovatively define the strain-ratio key (ε 1 /ε 2 , ε 2 /ε 3 , ε 3 /ε 4 ) induced by distinct bending states as the intrinsic unclonable hardware secret key, and construct a 4-bit combined coding scheme based on four distinguishable photocurrent levels modulated by these strain ratios to realize secure transmission of the message “FJIRSM.” This strain ratio-based system avoids complex optical modulation, ensuring ultrahigh security, and expands the application of two-dimensional ferroelectrics in advanced encrypted optoelectronics.

10.1002/adma.75366.title: Spatially Decoupled Cascade Oxygen Reduction on Bi Single-Atom and Cluster-Hybrid Sites for Hydroxyl Radical Generation
10.1002/adma.75366.abstract: ABSTRACT The two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) for H 2 O 2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O 2 activation and H 2 O 2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade-off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single-atom and cluster-hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand-exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal-organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co-anchored on B-doped TiO 2 . The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H 2 O 2 -to-·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free-energy diagrams indicate that H 2 O 2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p-band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h −1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3-9). Moreover, it enables broad-spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow-cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single-atom and cluster-hybrid interfaces.

10.1002/adma.75359.title: Sustained-Release Regulation on FAPbI 3 Crystallization to Enhance Photo-Thermal Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75359.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling crystallization kinetics of FAPbI 3 perovskite is crucial for improving crystal quality, device performance and stability. Herein, we report a sustained-release strategy to regulate the PbI 2 -to-FAPbI 3 conversion. PbI 2 lattice expansion arising from the interaction between PEI (oligomeric poly(ethyleneimine)) and iodide species suppresses nonuniform PbI 2 crystallization and facilitates FAI infiltration. Moreover, the weak interaction between oligomeric PEGDE (poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether) and FAI slows the reaction between FAI and PbI 2 , leading to homogeneous phase conversion during annealing. Consequently, enlarged FAPbI 3 grains are obtained with improved crystallographic orientation, reduced strain and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Furthermore, released PEI and PEGDE undergo in situ crosslinking to form a three-dimensional network that passivates grain boundaries, stabilizes microstructure and affords inner encapsulation. The resulting champion n-i-p device presents a power conversion efficiency of 26.6% (certified 26.17%). Both films and devices exhibit enhanced photothermal stability. The PEI/PEGDE-treated device maintains 92% of its initial efficiency at 85 °C for over 1,100 h, 96% after continuous illumination (∼100 mW cm − 2 ) and maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking for over 1,500 h, and 89% after MPP tracking at 85 °C over 12 days. This work offers a polymerization-assisted route for synchronizing crystallization control, defect passivation and inner encapsulation to enhance perovskite solar-cell stability.

10.1002/adma.75340.title: Albumin Orchestrates Type-I ROS Conversion for Efficient Intracellular Bacterial Clearance
10.1002/adma.75340.abstract: ABSTRACT Type-I photosensitization addresses the dilemma of intracellular bacterial hypoxia-induced photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) inefficacy, yet precise targeting and eradicating sequestered pathogens remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we engineer an albumin-based photodynamic conversion nanoparticles integrating target-specific recognition with controlled antibacterial functions to precisely eliminate intracellular pathogens and restore infected cell activity. Mechanistic studies reveal a vertically-crossed conformation that promotes intramolecular electron transfer and charge separation, redirecting photosensitizer (PS) reactivity toward type-I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Electron-rich albumin further enhances cationic PS +• recycling, photostability, and O 2 −• production, while its selective cytoplasmic delivery via receptor/charge interactions enables preferential accumulation in intracellular bacteria, with reduced off-target organelle engagement. We demonstrate application in S. aureus -infected sepsis showing high type-I ROS levels for antibacterial function from the nanoparticles to restore redox and immune homeostasis without noticeable toxicity. This work pioneers a conformationally-gated ROS conversion approach for eliminating intracellular bacterial infections, merging mechanistic precision with therapeutic potential for clinical sepsis management.

10.1002/adma.75322.title: Photonic Klein Tunnelling in Silicon Topological Materials for Terahertz 6G Interconnects
10.1002/adma.75322.abstract: ABSTRACT Topological photonics enables robust light transport along engineered interfaces, but transport across a potential barrier placed within such an interface, and the range of barrier strengths over which it survives, remain largely unexplored. Here we experimentally demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling in a Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. A local, inversion-symmetric barrier is introduced into a valley kink channel, with its strength Δ controlled through the geometry of the triangular holes. The barrier strength is calibrated using the local Dirac-frequency shift, establishing a direct relation between photonic crystal geometry and the effective tight-binding potential. We find that transmission remains close to its barrier-free value for Δ below the nearest-neighbour hopping amplitude t , and is strongly suppressed as Δ approaches t . Momentum-space analysis shows valley pseudospin preserved to better than 98% across two cascaded barriers. We further demonstrate Klein-tunnelling transport through multibarrier, Ω-shaped and power-splitter devices, supporting terahertz data transmission at rates up to 100 Gbit s − 1 . Our findings underpin a new design framework for resilient and high-capacity terahertz photonic integrated circuits.

10.1002/adma.75353.title: Topochemical Engineering of Two-Dimensional MXenes and Beyond
10.1002/adma.75353.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) materials have gained tremendous attention for their structural diversity and versatile functionality. However, conventional synthesis and post-synthetic modification often provide limited control over where and how structural or chemical changes occur, restricting the precise tailoring of composition, atomic configuration, and electronic structure. Topochemical engineering offers a distinct approach by directing chemical reactions at predefined sites while preserving key structural features of parent materials, thereby enabling precise and selective modulation at the atomic and molecular levels through four core strategies: conversion, termination, substitution, and transformation. Herein, we present a systematic and critical review of the latest advances in the topochemical engineering of MXenes and other representative 2D materials (TE-2DMs). We establish the conceptual framework and classification criteria for these strategies and discuss their implementation and underlying structural regulation mechanisms. Special emphasis is placed on the structure-performance correlations of TE-2DMs in electrochemical energy storage and conversion. We further summarize general design principles and practical guidelines for selecting and implementing appropriate topochemical strategies. Finally, we identify key challenges and emerging opportunities in this rapidly evolving field, with the aim of guiding the rational design of high-performance 2D functional materials for next-generation electrochemical energy technologies.

10.1002/adma.75352.title: Vacancy-Associated La-Ir Pairs Enable Water-Derived Oxygen-Hydroxyl Coupling for Durable Low-Ir PEM Water Electrolysis
10.1002/adma.75352.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly stable, low-iridium catalysts is critical for acidic oxygen evolution, but is limited by structural degradation driven by acid corrosion and voltage polarization. Herein, we report an iridium and lanthanum co-doped manganese-cobalt spinel catalyst, Ir,La-MCO δ , featuring octahedral La-Ir pairs (La oct -Ir oct ) with a theoretical favorable configuration of adjacent bridging and Ir z -axis oxygen vacancies. This low-Ir catalyst Ir,La-MCO δ (0.12 mg Ir cm −2 ) exhibits an overpotential of merely 220 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in pH = 1 electrolyte, and demonstrates robust operation for over 1550 h at 1 A cm −2 in a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer. Coupled (quasi)in situ characterizations and operando spectroscopy reveal that the adjacent oxygen vacancies mediate the evolution of oxygen intermediates, enabling water-derived oxygen-hydroxyl coupling with negligible lattice oxygen involvement, via a decoupled proton-electron transfer pathway.
