Co/CuNC, containing atomically dispersed Co and Cu sites within a nitrogen-doped carbon (NC), achieves a total C─N faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%, dominated by urea (20 ± 2%) and ethyl urea (16 ± 2%), with respective yield rates (YR) of 295 ± 25 and 50 ± 5 mmol h −1 g cat −1 . In situ synchrotron x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals potential-dependent changes in Cu and Co oxidation states and coordination environments, while in situ infrared spectroscopy identifies pulse-regulated *CO and *NH x intermediates and suggests concurrent electrochemical and Wöhler-type pathways. Density functional theory calculations reveal complementary site functions: Cu favors *NH 2 formation, whereas Co more strongly stabilizes *NH x and *CO intermediates, with *CO also accessible at Cu sites. These findings establish temporal coordination of reactant activation, intermediate populations, and active-site states as a mode-enabled strategy for accessing higher-order C─N products.

10.1002/adma.75346.title: Demagnetization-Driven Nanoscale Chirality-Selective Phonon Transport
10.1002/adma.75346.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral-lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality-selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality-selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α-SiO 2 . Using magneto-optic thermometry, we show that the effective thermal conductivity of α-SiO 2 depends systematically on both the magnetization direction of [Co/Pt] and the structural handedness of α-SiO 2 . This behavior is supported by first-principles-based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality-dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral-material interface. The magnetization-dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon-phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral-material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.

10.1002/adma.75324.title: Iron-Induced Interfacial Electronic Asymmetry Steers Pathway Divergence in Cobalt-Centered Fenton-Like Catalysis
10.1002/adma.75324.abstract: ABSTRACT Deep mineralization and matrix tolerance are difficult to reconcile in advanced oxidation processes because radical and nonradical pathways are often coupled in a composition-defined paradigm. Although multimetal materials can catalyze both pathways, the parallel reactions typically occur at different active sites, and their relative contributions are often governed by catalyst composition and active-site distribution, making deliberate regulation of pathway competition difficult. Here, we propose a multimetal catalyst with an electronically asymmetric Fe─O─Co interface to enable pathway divergence within a Co-centered catalytic environment. Fe introduction into CoNi layered hydroxides leads to electron density redistribution at neighboring Co sites and shifts PMS activation from a high-valent Co IV ═O-biased route toward a sulfate-radical-enriched regime while retaining complementary nonradical oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved 1.43-fold greater TOC removal and a 1.47-fold higher PMS utilization efficiency (PUE) for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation than the Fe-free control, with robust decontamination performance against common background matrix interference and sustained activity over 96 h of high-flux continuous-flow operation. This work establishes interfacial Fe regulation as a pathway-engineering strategy for steering oxidant-activation selectivity through heterometal-induced electronic asymmetry, providing a route to reconcile mineralization depth with matrix tolerance in Fenton-like water treatment.

10.1002/adma.75143.title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
10.1002/adma.75143.abstract: ABSTRACT Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy-corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low-defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), carrier density (5.73 × 10 20 cm −3 ), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8-14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large-scale processability and outstanding long-term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

10.1002/adma.75316.title: Fano-Engineered Au@Se Core-Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual-Mode Structural Color
10.1002/adma.75316.abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate-free and solution-processable, but single-component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core-shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible-range Mie-resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano-like interference between the broad electric-dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au-core electric-dipole response. The hybrid mode yields Q factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single-component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)-curable resins and writing inks for 254-ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization-selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive-index coating.

10.1002/adma.75380.title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
10.1002/adma.75380.abstract: ABSTRACT The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI-driven techniques, and other high-tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross-contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal-ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1-Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene-containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1-Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape-changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1-Ru1 can be recycled via a one-pot, cross-contamination-free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high-tech applications.

10.1002/adma.75342.title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane-Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells
10.1002/adma.75342.abstract: ABSTRACT The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial-derived double-layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell-free carriers, fused with cell-penetrating peptide-modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan-microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut-associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune-stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select Bifidobacterium bifidum -derived oral vaccine combined with anti-PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1-, Th17-immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long-term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon-γ-producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole-3-acetic-acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T-cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite-driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.

10.1002/adma.75197.title: Enhanced Bulk Photovoltaics in Polar 2D Hybrid Perovskite via Pressure-Strengthened Organic-Inorganic Interactions
10.1002/adma.75197.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in polar two-dimensional (2D) organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites (OIHPs) is currently impeded by an insufficient understanding of the microscopic mechanisms linking organic-inorganic interactions to photovoltaic output. Here, we utilize pressure as an effective thermodynamic probe to decouple these interactions in BDA(EA) 2 Pb 3 Br 10 (BDA is 1,4-butanediammonium, EA is ethylammonium), achieving the first pressure-engineered synergistic enhancement of short-circuit current ( I SC ) and open-circuit voltage ( V OC ). Comprehensive in situ characterizations reveal that pressure-strengthened N─H···Br hydrogen bonding induces cooperative organic cation ordering and inorganic octahedral distortion. This structural synergy amplifies spontaneous polarization, resulting in a 530-fold increase in BPVE efficiency to 0.18% at 1.5 GPa, a value surpassing all previously reported OIHPs. Moreover, the enhanced organic-inorganic interaction stabilizes the ferroelectric state, elevating the Curie temperature to 433 K. These results elucidate the microscopic mechanism underlying BPVE enhancement in 2D OIHP ferroelectrics and establish pressure modulation as an effective strategy for mechanistic studies and photovoltaic optimization.

10.1002/adma.75223.title: In Situ Ordered Glassification of Gels for Exceptional Stiffness and Toughness
10.1002/adma.75223.abstract: ABSTRACT Glassy gels are indispensable for applications ranging from structural composites to bioelectronics, yet their design is plagued by an intrinsic paradox where the rigid molecular constraints that endow high stiffness simultaneously restrict polymer chain dynamics, precluding the energy dissipation mechanisms essential for toughness. Here, we circumvent this fundamental trade-off through an in situ molecular constraint-induced ordered glassification strategy. By restricting localized conformations within a confined hydration environment, we drive the spontaneous assembly of long-range ordered, load-bearing nanodomains within a soft gel matrix. These domains function as rigid sacrificial units during initial deformation. Critically, they undergo a progressive, strain-activated dissociation that redistributes local stress and dissipates mechanical energy at the bulk scale. Unlike conventional post-treated gels, our material undergoes a rubbery-to-glassy transition in situ without external intervention, yielding a 3500-fold modulus enhancement and a toughness of 289 MJ m −3 , exceeding many reported high-modulus hydrogels and ionic gels. Furthermore, this molecular design imparts multimodal functionality, including strong yet water-removable adhesion (∼17 MPa to glass), superior impact resistance, and water-responsive shape programmability. This ordered glassification paradigm establishes a versatile molecular engineering route to create load-bearing gels that synergistically integrate stiffness, toughness, and adaptive intelligence, redefining the performance envelope of hydrated soft matter.

10.1002/adma.75184.title: Active Soft Hydrogels Reveal Cumulative Molecular Force Dosing in Stem Cell Fate Programming
10.1002/adma.75184.abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling molecular-scale mechanical signaling from bulk substrate stiffness remains a fundamental challenge in biomaterial design. Here, we develop a soft-yet-active hyaluronic acid hydrogel (∼3 kPa) grafted with near-infrared-driven CD-PNIPAM-RGD molecular actuators to apply programmable, piconewton-scale forces directly to integrins without altering the bulk modulus. By isolating force history as an independent variable, we reveal that human mesenchymal stem cells act as cumulative mechanical integrators. A cumulative force dose of just 7 h (1-h daily pulses) drives irreversible osteogenic commitment on this classically non-permissive substrate. Mechanistically, each pulse bypasses canonical tension-based signaling. Despite negligible cytoplasmic traction, localized molecular pulling drives G-actin nuclear import, intranuclear F-actin polymerization, and rapid YAP activation. By recasting mechanotransduction from a continuous analog response into a discrete, cumulative integration of mechanical inputs, this work establishes active force dosing as a quantitative design principle for next-generation soft biomaterials.

10.1002/adma.75103.title: Giant Nonequilibrium Valley Control via Spin-Selective Hot-Carrier Transfer in an Antiferromagnetic van der Waals Stack
10.1002/adma.75103.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-selective hot-carrier transfer at interfaces between two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors and magnets offers a nonequilibrium route to manipulate spin and valley degrees of freedom. In van der Waals heterostructures, such transfer can be enabled by type-III band alignment together with magnetic-field-induced spin polarization of the bands in adjacent magnetic layers. Yet, continuous and robust valley control with high magnetic-field susceptibility remains challenging, particularly beyond binary switching in out-of-plane easy-axis magnets. Here we fabricate a CrSBr/WSe 2 /CrSBr heterostructure, where two semiconductor-magnet interfaces promote efficient hot-carrier transfer. Utilizing valley-resolved magneto-photoluminescence spectroscopy, we reveal a pronounced field-sign-asymmetric response and a magnetic-state-dependent evolution of emergent spectral features that track the spin configuration of multilayer CrSBr via spin-selective hot-carrier transfer. This mechanism enables giant, continuous tuning, and magnetic-state-dependent reversal of the degree of circular polarization (DoCP), reaching ∼ 40% for excitons and ∼ 80% for trion emission. Our results establish spin-polarized interlayer hot-carrier transfer as an efficient knob for engineering valley polarization and coherence in TMDs, and highlight antiferromagnet-based stacks as a versatile platform for magnetically programmable quantum optoelectronic functionalities.

10.1002/adma.74151.title: Stimuli-Responsive Hierarchical Structuring Controls Survival and Programs Hydrogelation of Supramolecular Metallofibers
authors: Merlin R. Stühler, László Mérai, Kai Ludwig, Rainer Haag, Quinn A. Besford, Alex J. Plajer

10.1002/adma.75385.title: Turning Nd-Fe-B Swarf Into High-Value Bulk Feedstocks via Sustainable Hydrogen Plasma: From Rare-Earth Oxides to Metals and Hydrides
10.1002/adma.75385.abstract: ABSTRACT Rare-earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and other high-efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy-intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare-earth elements (REEs) content (∼20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we achieve phase separation into metallic Fe and a Nd 2 O 3 -rich rare-earth fraction, providing a concentrated intermediate for subsequent REPM production. The process also enables direct rare-earth hydride formation, confirming the plasma-assisted partial rare-earth metallization in the molten state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high-value, high-purity feedstock in a single, acid-free step. Against the ∼70 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 footprint of conventional REPM production, this recycling route offers a pathway toward substantially lower-emission magnet production while reducing reliance on primary REE supply.

10.1002/adma.75302.title: A Universal Spin-Polarization-Engineered Antibonding-Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh-Rate Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75302.abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion-type anode materials hold great promise for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass-transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal-chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long-standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin-polarization-engineered (SPE) antibonding-orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh-rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin-state transition from low-spin to high-spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin-engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn-FeS 2 /CoS 2 anode delivers an ultrahigh-rate capability of 300 mA h g −1 at 120 A g −1 , together with exceptional long-term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g −1 ), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial-level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.

10.1002/adma.75321.title: Nonlinear Electro-Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid-State Quantum Defects
10.1002/adma.75321.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrated visible photonic engines for solid-state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt-scale visible light generation and high-contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip-scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high-fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz-bandwidth electro-optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off-chip green-light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time-resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time-tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high-speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high-rate quantum communication nodes.

10.1002/adma.74305.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Design of High-Entropy Oxide Catalysts
10.1002/adma.74305.abstract: ABSTRACT High-entropy oxides (HEOs), which contain multiple cations with diverse valence states and highly disordered local environments, offer a much broader compositional and active-site space than conventional single-component oxides. This diversity creates opportunities for tailoring catalytic properties, but it also makes rational design considerably more difficult. The formation and stability of HEOs phases depend on the combined effects of configurational entropy, mixing enthalpy, oxidation potential, valence compatibility, and synthesis conditions. Meanwhile, their catalytic behavior is often controlled by oxygen vacancies, surface segregation, in situ reconstruction, and dynamically evolving active sites under operating conditions. Artificial intelligence (AI) provides a promising means of managing this complexity by learning relationships among composition, structure, defects, adsorption behavior, and catalytic performance. This review summarizes the major challenges in HEOs catalyst design, discusses data representation and model selection, and examines AI applications in phase stability prediction, hydrogen production, oxygen evolution, thermal catalysis, photocatalysis, and electrocatalyst discovery. It further emphasizes the need to move beyond single-property prediction toward multi-objective optimization and closed-loop integration of AI, DFT, MLIP-based sampling, operando characterization, and experimental validation.

10.1002/adma.75392.title: Synchronized Ablation of Multifocal Tumors Enabled by Multi-Channel Lanthanide Nanocomposites
10.1002/adma.75392.abstract: ABSTRACT The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi-channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH-responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione-responsive near-infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature-responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole-body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.

10.1002/adma.74197.title: Structural Design Strategies of Sustainable Wood-Derived Solar-Driven Interfacial Evaporator for Advancing Water Purification
10.1002/adma.74197.abstract: ABSTRACT High energy consumption poses a significant limitation to conventional water purification technologies. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) has emerged as a sustainable alternative. Wood, endowed with its inherent hierarchical porous structure, exceptional hydrophilicity, low thermal conductivity, and biocompatibility, stands out as an ideal substrate for SDIE. When used in SDIE, wood not only reduces embodied carbon by substituting energy-intensive materials but also continues to store biogenic carbon throughout its service life, thereby lowering the device's overall carbon footprint. This review synthesizes research advances in wood-based SDIE (W-SDIE), focusing on structural design strategies for performance enhancement. Specifically, it elaborates on the advantages of wood's microstructure and chemical composition as a substrate; summarizes performance optimization approaches across three dimensions: heat management (light absorber design, insulating structure, and environmental energy harvesting), water management (water transport pathway, wettability regulation, and evaporation enthalpy reduction), and salt management (water-salt transport regulation, salt-oriented crystallization, and self-cleaning mechanism); and outlines applications in desalination, wastewater treatment, photocatalytic degradation, and energy coupling. Ultimately, current challenges and potential solutions are discussed, providing insights for the future development of W-SDIE.

10.1002/adma.75381.title: Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics: From Anatomical Access to Disease-Focused Applications
10.1002/adma.75381.abstract: ABSTRACT Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation-mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter-based, ocular, or intra-articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site-specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease-focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth-factor supplementation, local antibody-fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat-dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.

10.1002/adma.75368.title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation-Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors
10.1002/adma.75368.abstract: ABSTRACT Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect-mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path-dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles ( n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full-cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation-mediated nucleation and orientation-regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

10.1002/adma.75371.title: All-In-One Integration of Inherently Flame-Retardant, UV-Resistant, and Antibacterial Polymer by a Biguanide Unit
10.1002/adma.75371.abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra-efficient strategy to achieve the all-in-one integration of inherently flame-retardant, UV-resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high-temperature char-formation for flame retardance, n →π* transition absorption for UV-resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide-containing polymer material achieves the best UL-94 V-0 flame-retardant rating with excellent self-extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra-high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely-existed bacteria.

10.1002/adma.75388.title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion-Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75388.abstract: ABSTRACT Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate-phase film with a Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two-step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums-based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm 2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1-sun illumination (ISOS-L-2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.

10.1002/adma.75400.title: Magnetic-Field-Annealing-Induced Short-Range Order in High-Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response
10.1002/adma.75400.abstract: ABSTRACT The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO-supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of −72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature-specific maxima. Local microscopy, field-associated atomistic modeling, and fixed-composition electronic-structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co-centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.

10.1002/adma.75369.title: Nonreciprocal Bending in Ferroelectric Membranes Driven by Flexoelectricity
10.1002/adma.75369.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi-static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single-crystalline PbTiO 3 membrane using suspended-membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity-dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase-field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.

10.1002/adma.75413.title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium-Free Acidic Water Oxidation
10.1002/adma.75413.abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of noble metal-free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity-stability trade-off, wherein non-precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium-stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu 0.08 Co 2.92 O 4 ) designed through site-specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu-O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co-O covalency and suppresses Co 2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co-Co distance to favor direct O-O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu 0.08 Co 2.92 O 4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm −2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm −2 , highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.

10.1002/adma.75412.title: An Ultrarobust Dual-Modal Neural Fiber With In-Sensor Computing
10.1002/adma.75412.abstract: ABSTRACT Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human-machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in-sensor-computing dual-modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness-sustaining 300 times load-bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in-sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real-time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material-architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual-modality, and in-sensor computing, setting the stage for next-generation wearable human-machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.

10.1002/adma.74642.title: TESCLA: A Fully Soft Electromagnetic Linear Actuator With Continuous Bending Enabled by Liquid-Metal Solenoids
10.1002/adma.74642.abstract: ABSTRACT Linear actuators are widely employed in robots and wearable devices due to their capability of directly generating linear motion. Although soft actuators and flexible linear actuators have been developed to enable effective operation in various configurations, they are still constrained by a limited actuation range and a discrete bending, which restricts their achievable workspace and curvatures. Here, we propose a tubular electromagnetic soft conformal linear actuator (TESCLA) exerting thrust force over a large actuation stroke with continuous bending. The actuator operates under both a straight configuration and a conformal deformation to the surrounding environment, leveraging the softness of liquid-metal solenoids (soft stator) and compliant magnetic composites (soft mover). The synchronous actuation strategy allows the actuator to produce controllable bidirectional electromagnetic thrust by applying an electric current to the soft stator. In addition, the step position is estimated by measuring inductance variance of the soft solenoids resulting from the displacement of the soft mover. The design of the actuator components is evaluated through numerical simulations to determine an effective configuration, considering performance characteristics such as thrust force, minimum step size, and sensing resolution. By utilizing the functionalities of the proposed actuator, biomimetic robotic applications and a wearable haptic device were demonstrated.

10.1002/adma.74942.title: Discovery of Multicomponent Invar Materials With Low Thermal Expansion, High Curie Temperature, and Superior Phase Stability Assisted by Active Learning
10.1002/adma.74942.abstract: ABSTRACT Zero thermal expansion (ZTE) materials provide exceptional dimensional stability under temperature fluctuations, making them indispensable for high-precision instrumentation and extreme environments. However, their natural scarcity, combined with the vast compositional space in multicomponent systems, renders traditional trial-and-error approaches both time-consuming and cost-prohibitive, posing an emergent challenge for modern high-tech applications. Here, we establish a task-specific active-learning framework with empirical fine-tuning to accelerate ZTE materials' design. By mining sparse experimental datasets, we identified a high-potential compositional region and uncovered several novel low-expansion alloys. Among them, Cr 1.4 Co 8.9 Ni 30.5 Fe 59 exhibits a low coefficient of thermal expansion of , and a high Curie temperature reaching 580 . Real-time in situ neutron and synchrotron x-ray diffraction confirm its single-phase face-centered cubic structure, excellent ductility, and robust phase stability against thermal and mechanical stimuli. Crucially, machine learning analysis pinpointed six key descriptors highly correlated with low-expansion performance, providing data-driven insights into the magnetovolume origins of this behavior. This work not only yields a high-performance dimensionally stable alloy, but also demonstrates how integrating physical insights with data-driven design can accelerate advanced materials development.

10.1002/aenm.71681.title: Pore-Stitching Engineering of Biomass-Derived Hard Carbon for Enhanced Sodium-Ion Storage
10.1002/aenm.71681.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass-derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising and cost-effective anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Prior to carbonization, biomass precursors are commonly subjected to acid/alkali purification to remove metallic and non-metallic impurities. However, the accompanying ionic etching process often generates abundant through-pores and disrupts the carbon framework, leading to increased irreversible capacity loss. Herein, we propose a “pore stitching” strategy using hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a functional reconstruction precursor. The hydroxyl-rich HEC is proposed to interact with oxygen-containing sites in the demineralized precursor and to be retained within accessible pore regions during mixing and drying. During subsequent carbonization, HEC-derived carbon contributes to the reconstruction of the disrupted carbon framework, resulting in reduced open surface exposure and a redistributed micro/ultramicroporous architecture while preserving favorable Na + storage domains. Consequently, the optimized HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 375.3 mAh g − 1 at 20 mA g − 1 . A 700 mAh pouch cell pairing this HC with sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 , NFPP) delivers 150 Wh kg − 1 based on the combined active-material mass of both electrodes and retains 97.8% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a viable route for converting impurity-rich agricultural waste into high-performance HC anodes for practical sodium-ion energy storage.

10.1002/aenm.71695.title: Dual Descriptor-Guided Design of Hydrated Eutectic Electrolytes for Stable Zinc Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71695.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise large-scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen-bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H 2 O activity and regulate Zn 2+ desolvation through hydrogen-bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol-based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen-bond network formation and Zn 2+ coordination. A series of C 2 -C 6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen-bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C 4 , EOD = 0.022 Å −3 , MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery-enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm −2 with 1 mAh cm −2 , and the Zn||I 2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.

10.1002/aenm.71700.title: Jahn-Teller Distortion of MnO 6 Octahedra Enhances Piezoelectric Polarization and Lattice Oxygen Activation of BaTiO 3 for Efficient Piezo-PEC Water Splitting
10.1002/aenm.71700.abstract: ABSTRACT Piezo-photoelectrochemical (Piezo-PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water-splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn-Teller effect-driven strategy to regulate the local B-site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO 3 for efficient Piezo-PEC water splitting. By introducing Mn 3+ ions with asymmetric e g orbital occupancy (t 2g 3 e g 1 ), a local MnO 6 octahedral coordination environment is constructed and pronounced Jahn-Teller distortion is induced. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn-Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non-centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn 3+ strengthens Ti─O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water-splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) toward the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), thus accelerating reaction kinetics. Under coupled ultrasonic vibration and illumination, the optimized BTMO-6 photoanode delivers a high photocurrent density of 2.18 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE and exhibits a piezoelectric coefficient (d 33 ) of 52.3 pm V −1 . This work reveals that Jahn-Teller distortion simultaneously enhances piezo-polarization and tunes reaction pathways, offering new insights for robust Piezo-PEC water-splitting systems.

10.1002/aenm.71693.title: Nickel-Free Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Self-Assembled Monolayers: A Pathway to Efficient and Recyclable Devices
10.1002/aenm.71693.abstract: ABSTRACT High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel-containing hole-selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross-contamination during end-of-life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel-free hole-selective interface material based on phenyl-substituted phosphonic-acid carbazole self-assembled monolayers (Ph-nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure-property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph-5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried-interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me-4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph-5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel-free interface enables a closed-loop recycling route unavailable to nickel-based devices, with recycled-ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life-cycle and techno-economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity-related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.

10.1002/aenm.71692.title: Photoelectrochemical Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion: Cocatalyst Design Principles and Mechanistic Insights from Electrocatalysis
10.1002/aenm.71692.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO 3 RR) offers a solar-driven route to NH 3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value-added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO 3 RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO 3 RR research has produced an extensive library of high-performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO 3 RR, spanning light-absorber engineering, photoelectrode-cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO 3 RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge-transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH 3 synthesis.

10.1002/aenm.71688.title: Gravity-Differential Modulated Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Continuous and Stable Energy Harvesting From Disordered Vibrations
10.1002/aenm.71688.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self-powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity-differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM-TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity-driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM-TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher-frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double-sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM-TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long-term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM-TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self-powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.

10.1002/aenm.71690.title: Molecular Architecture of Non-Fullerene Acceptors Balances Homo- and Hetero-Intermolecular Interactions to Enhance Thermal Stability of Organic Photovoltaics
10.1002/aenm.71690.abstract: ABSTRACT High-efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor-acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo- and hetero-intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well-known indacenodithieno[3,2- b ]thiophene-based (ITIC-series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene-based (IEICO-series) acceptors, and state-of-the-art Y-series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo-interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine-tune their hetero-interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo-interactions while minimizing hetero-interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature-reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo- and hetero-interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.

10.1002/aenm.71652.title: Local Atomic Disorder-Driven Deep Relaxor State for Ultrahigh Dielectric Energy Storage With High Thermal Stability
10.1002/aenm.71652.abstract: ABSTRACT Lead-free dielectric ceramic capacitors are indispensable for advanced high-power electronic pulse systems owing to their exceptional power density and rapid charge-discharge kinetics. However, the simultaneous realization of ultrahigh recoverable energy density ( W rec ) and high efficiency ( η ), especially with robust thermal stability, remains challenging. Here, we propose a local structural design strategy focused on implementing atomic-scale disorder within relaxor ferroelectrics to achieve a deep relaxor state across a wide temperature window. Atomic-scale structure characterizations reveal that this local chemical/structural disorder induces ultrafine, highly active polar nanoregions, fostering an optimized polarization response while remaining resilient against thermal fluctuations. Consequently, the designed ceramics exhibit superior energy-storage performance, characterized by a large W rec of 13.1 J cm −3 and ultrahigh η of 93%, leading to a high figure of merit up to 187.1. Notably, exceptional performance stability across diverse operating conditions is bestowed, with η remaining above 90% at temperatures up to 200°C. This study thus provides a robust paradigm for designing dielectric capacitors that deliver both high energy-storage performance and reliability in harsh working environments.
authors: Bing Xie, Yuhang Hu, Wenqiang Xiang, Zhiyong Liu, Kun Guo, Haibo Zhang, Huajie Luo, Tianyu Li

10.1002/aenm.71686.title: Ni-MOFs Mediated Ni2+/4+ Balancing and Enhanced Metal-Oxygen Covalency Unlocks Fast and Stable Sodium Storage in High-Entropy Layered Cathode
10.1002/aenm.71686.abstract: ABSTRACT O3-type cathodes suffer from heterogeneous metal distribution and insufficient active nickel content, limiting specific capacity, cyclic stability, and electrochemical kinetics. Herein, Ni-based metal-organic frameworks (Ni-MOFs) are applied as precursors to enable atomic-level control over regulated active nickel content and metal-oxygen bonds in high-entropy NaTMO 2 cathodes. It is found that the introduction of Ni-MOFs can accelerate the crystallization and purity of O3-type structures. Ni-MOFs-derived high-entropy cathode (M-HEO) exhibits an optimized electrochemically active Ni 2+ , which can balance the capacity depth and structural stability, contrasting with excessive Ni 2+ in normal high-entropy oxide or insufficient Ni 2+ in commercial oxide. Concurrently, enhanced transition metal-oxygen covalency, especially Ni-O covalency, could form a robust metal-oxygen network with an ultrafast Na + transport path and suppress lattice degradation. The reinforced covalent Ni-O-TM network enables a highly reversible phase transition with a small volume change, as well as the modified, thinner double-layer cathode-electrolyte interface, together with fast Na + ion transport kinetics. As a result, M-HEO delivers a higher discharge capacity of ∼130 mAh g −1 with an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.6% under 0.1C and stable cyclic property under 1C and 2C.
authors: Shengkui Zhong, Bo Yang, Jishu Zeng, Xingyu Luo, Jiequn Liu, Zejun Jiang, Yanfang Wang, Fangping Wang, Xueling Hu, Huijue Luo, Yan Su, Zongkang Sun, Zhuokui Zhong, Shibao Tang, Renzong Hu, Wei Li, Fanbo Meng

10.1002/aenm.71691.title: Counter-Halide-Directed Ion-Pair Passivation Enables High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71691.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (PVSK) are key top-cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics but remain limited by severe open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) losses and photoinduced halide segregation. Since iodide- and bromide-related defects coexist at the surface and bulk of Br/I mixed-halide WBG PVSK, the counter-halide identity in ammonium passivators may critically influence defect passivation effectiveness. Moreover, while deprotonation of ammonium passivator has emerged as an important factor governing interfacial stability, its discussion has focused mainly on organic cation structure, leaving the counter-halide's role in regulating deprotonation-driven side reactions largely unexplored. Here, we establish a counter-halide-directed ion-pair passivation strategy using 4-fluorobenzylammonium halides (FBz-Cl, FBz-Br, and FBz-I). Density functional theory calculations combined with optoelectronic and interfacial characterizations reveal that the counter-halide simultaneously governs defect-binding affinity, nonradiative recombination, energy-level alignment, and deprotonation-driven degradation. Among the passivators, FBz-Br achieves the optimal balance of strong defect passivation, favorable band alignment with C 60 , and enhanced stability. Consequently, FBz-Br-treated PVSK exhibits suppressed nonradiative recombination and reduced V OC deficit, delivering a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.89% with improved resistance to moisture, thermal, and light-induced degradation. Integrated with Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) bottom cells, the optimized WBG PVSK enables PVSK/CIGS tandem solar cells with PCEs of 29.51% in four-terminal and 25.65% in two-terminal configurations.

10.1002/aenm.71694.title: Calendering-Dependent Electrochemical and Cost-Energy Tradeoffs in Layered - Olivine Blend Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71694.abstract: ABSTRACT Blended cathodes comprised of layered oxide and olivine materials, such as LiNi 0.9 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (NMC) and LiMn 0.7 Fe 0.3 PO 4 (LMFP), are appealing due to their reduced cost and enhanced safety, rate capability, and cyclability compared to high-Ni layered oxides. However, while these blends are often discussed in terms of particle-level properties, the effect of processing conditions, such as calendering, has received less attention, despite their strong influence on electrode microstructure due to the differences in morphology, surface characteristics, and crystallographic density. We investigate here systematically NMC, NMC/LMFP with 70/30 wt.%, and NMC/LMFP with 50/50 wt.% cathodes under uncalendered, moderately-calendered, and hard-calendered conditions, employing state-of-charge-dependent rate analysis, full-cell cycling, electrode-level transport characterization, and cathode-level cost-energy evaluation. NMC tolerates calendering, maintaining rate capability, while showing improved capacity retention over 500 cycles. In contrast, NMC/LMFP blends show a narrower, composition-dependent calendering limit. The 70/30 blend retains its rate-capability benefit under no-to-moderate calendering, whereas the 50/50 blend is strongly penalized by densification. Hard calendering induces transport-limited behavior in the blends, eliminating rate benefits and degrading cyclability. Stabilizing the NMC with Nb incorporation further improves cyclability and energy retention of the 70/30 blend, demonstrating a pathway to combine microstructure-enabled rate capability with improved durability and favorable cathode-level cost-energy balance.
authors: Huyen T. K. Nguyen, Arumugam Manthiram

10.1002/aenm.71677.title: Unlocking Three-Dimensional Electron and Ion Transport in High-Loading and Dense Lithium-Ion Battery Electrodes Assisted via Porous Graphene Networks
10.1002/aenm.71677.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient electron and ion transport in high-loading, densely packed electrodes remains a major challenge for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries. Increasing mass loading extends transport pathways for both charge carriers, while electrode densification by roll pressing, essential for maximizing gravimetric and volumetric energy density and minimizing electrolyte content, further restricts ion transport in low-porosity electrodes. Here, graphene mesosponge (GMS) is introduced as a functional conductive additive that tailors electrode microstructure through its sponge-like mesoporous framework. High-loading electrodes based on Co-free, pure-Ni layered oxides containing only 1 wt.% GMS exhibit enhanced electronic and ionic conductivity, delivering high reversible capacity with reduced polarization. The deformable mesoporous framework of GMS also buffers compressive stress during roll pressing, enabling practical electrode densities above 3.5 g cm −3 without inducing cracking of the active material particles. Digital-twin analysis reveals that the porous GMS architecture forms a three-dimensional electron- and ion-transport network, with electrolyte retained within its mesopores facilitating ion transport and resulting in superior rate capability compared with electrodes containing single-walled carbon nanotubes. These results demonstrate that GMS is a transformative conductive additive for simultaneously improving energy and power densities in practical lithium-ion batteries through rational microstructural design of dense composite electrodes.
authors: Yosuke Ugata, Rei Matsumoto, Sera Sato, Jaejin Lim, Yong Min Lee, Hiroshi Ueda, Atsuo Omaru, Kosuke Ishii, Naoaki Yabuuchi

10.1002/aenm.71685.title: Catalytic Activity Matching Governs Scaffold-Coating Competition in Silicon Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71685.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon scaffolds are widely used to accommodate lithiation-induced volume changes of silicon (Si) nanoparticles and maintain electrode integrity, yet whether increasing scaffold rigidity provides sufficient mechanical benefit to offset its cost in surface coating quality remains unexamined. The scaffold template and the native SiO x on Si surfaces compete for the same finite carbon source, so that scaffold wall thickness and coating uniformity are inversely coupled rather than independently tunable. We formalize this coupling as catalytic activity matching and probe it using MgSO 4 and CaSO 4 whisker templates, whose activity contrast is quantified by density functional theory and H 2 temperature-programmed reduction. The high-activity MgSO 4 template diverts carbon flux toward the scaffold, leaving nonuniform Si coatings, whereas the moderate-activity CaSO 4 template yields a compliant scaffold with uniform coatings. The uniform coating governs solid electrolyte interphase quality, while the compliant scaffold reduces peak lithiation stress to only 53.4% of its rigid counterpart. The matched CaSO 4 system delivers 91.0% initial Coulombic efficiency and enables full cells up to 510 Wh kg −1 (based on the combined mass of active materials). Matching rather than maximizing template catalytic activity is thus established as a general design principle for balancing scaffold formation and Si-surface protection in template-catalyzed CVD.
authors: Yin Yang, Henglong Ren, Maoxin Cai, Xinlong Ma, Yongfeng Li

10.1002/aenm.71683.title: Macromolecular Design of Bipolar Donor-Acceptor Polymer Cathodes for Fast and Durable Aluminum Dual-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71683.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum dual-ion batteries (ADIBs) are promising for sustainable electrochemical energy storage, yet organic cathodes rarely combine efficient bipolar redox utilization, rapid charge transport, long-term durability, and operation at high mass loadings. Here, four phenothiazine-anthraquinone donor-acceptor polymers are constructed by varying chain architecture, D-A connectivity, and backbone rigidity to elucidate how macromolecular structure regulates bipolar charge storage. The resulting structure-transport relationships reveal that open crosslinked networks improve ion accessibility, whereas direct D-A conjugation within rigid backbones promotes orbital delocalization and charge transfer. These complementary structural features activate both p-type phenothiazine and n-type anthraquinone redox centers, enabling reversible co-storage of AlCl 4 − and AlCl 2+ . Accordingly, the optimized PTZAQ-C3 delivers a reversible capacity of 243 mAh g −1 , excellent rate capability (122 mAh g −1 at 50.0 A g −1 ), and exceptional cycling stability up to 90,000 cycles. PTZAQ-C3 also maintains 200 mAh g −1 at −30°C and reaches an areal capacity of 10.08 mAh cm −2 at a mass loading of 50.4 mg cm −2 . These findings highlight macromolecular design as a general strategy for developing high-performance bipolar organic cathodes for aluminum dual-ion and related multicarrier batteries.
authors: Wenyan Ma, Chong Zhang, Ran Zhou, Xiaoxiao Zhang, Can Liu, Zikang Deng, Ziming Tu, Xunliang Hu, Jia-Xing Jiang

10.1002/aenm.71680.title: Upcycling Strategy for Mixed Spent Batteries to Enable NMC622 & Graphite Full Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71680.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of lithium-ion batteries is intensifying pressure on critical-material supply chains while generating increasing volumes of complex battery waste. However, existing recycling technologies struggle to process mixed feedstocks efficiently and often recover products with limited added value. Here, we advance beyond cathode-focused hydrometallurgical recycling by integrating composition-adjustable cathode resynthesis with the purification and surface modification of co-recovered graphite, followed by full-pouch-cell validation and unified process-level assessment. Mixed low-nickel cathodes are upgraded to high-performance LiNi 0.6 Mn 0.2 Co 0.2 O 2 (NMC622) with improved lithium-ion transport and cycling stability. Meanwhile, a closed-loop graphite upcycling process produces battery-grade anodes with enhanced interfacial kinetics and durability. Full pouch cells assembled entirely from the upcycled materials exhibit fewer side reactions and approximately twice the cycle life of cells using commercial counterparts, retaining 70% of their capacity after 2590 cycles. Techno-economic and life-cycle analyses further indicate >95% recycled-material utilization, 22.9% higher profitability, and reductions of 27.0% in greenhouse-gas emissions and 29.4% in energy consumption relative to the reference recycling route. These findings establish mixed battery waste as a viable feedstock for producing high-value battery materials and demonstrate a pathway from conventional resource recovery toward value-added remanufacturing for circular, resilient, and low-carbon battery supply chains.
authors: Zeyi Yao, Jiahui Hou, Zifei Meng, Xiaotu Ma, Jinzhao Fu, Zexin Wang, Zhenzhen Yang, Jianguo Wen, Maksim Sultanov, Hari Adhikari, Yihao Shen, Geoffrey A. Tompsett, Yan Wang

10.1002/aenm.71654.title: Integrated d-p Orbital Coupling Within High-Entropy Oxide/Halloysite Accelerates Sulfur Reduction Kinetics in Sodium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71654.abstract: ABSTRACT The sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttle effect remains a major obstacle to achieving the high theoretical capacity of room-temperature sodium-sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries. Herein, the high-entropy oxide/halloysite nanotube hybrid host (HEO/HNT) is developed by integrating multicomponent catalytic sites with a naturally abundant 1D clay scaffold for efficient sulfur conversion. The hollow tubular structure of HNT enables uniform HEO anchoring and effective confinement of sulfur species, while the robust Si─O and Al─OH framework enhances cathode stability during long-term cycling. Density functional theory calculations reveal that interfacial coupling between the metal 3d orbitals of HEO and the Al/Si 3p orbitals of HNT induces extended orbital delocalization, thereby strengthening NaPSs adsorption and lowering the free energy barriers for stepwise polysulfide conversion. In situ and ex situ characterizations further verify accelerated NaPSs reduction kinetics and suppressed shuttling. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the S@HEO/HNT cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 1225 mAh g −1 after 450 cycles at 1 C and maintains 478 mAh g −1 over 2500 cycles at 10 C, corresponding to an ultralow capacity fading of 0.008% per cycle. This study bridges high-entropy oxide with naturally abundant clay substrates, offering a scalable route toward durable, high-rate RT Na-S batteries.
authors: Guangming Cao, Heng Zhang, Youcun Bai, Yingying Song, Lang Qiu, Xiang-Long Huang, Tao Song, Wei Sun, Chang Ming Li

10.1002/aenm.71687.title: Chloride-Mediated Photoelectrochemical Selective Oxidation of Polyols Coupled With Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/aenm.71687.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting coupled with the oxidation of polyols into high-value-added chemicals is of practical significance for the upgrading of biomass and polyester plastics. However, the current polyols selective oxidation reactions suffer from harsh reaction conditions (strong basic electrolyte) and high costs of noble metal-based catalyst via the reactive oxygen species-mediated pathway. Herein, we for the first time demonstrate a chlorine radicals-mediated route toward polyols oxidation under neutral conditions. As proof-of-concept, NiCo-LDH-decorated TiO 2 has been developed to promote the oxidation of ethylene glycol (EG) to glycolic acid (GA), achieving a GA production rate of 8.7 µmol cm -2 h -1 with a selectivity of 76.2% in NaCl electrolyte under irradiation, which is the highest value reported to date in PEC system. Mechanistic studies reveal that the key chlorine radicals facilitate C─H bond cleavage to form chlorinated intermediates for GA production. Additionally, we successfully coupled PEC PET-derived EG valorization with H 2 generation from seawater, attaining GA and H 2 productivity of 30.6 and 93.9 µmol cm -2 , respectively. This work offers a novel perspective on polyols oxidation reaction pathway modulation and demonstrates a solar-to-chemical conversion approach for integrating low-value carbon sources recycling and PEC synthesis.
authors: Lan Luo, Shanshan Zhang, Xiaomei Zhang, Yutong Cai, Wangsong Chen, Wenjing Dai, Haisong Feng, Zhen Yin, Zhenhua Li, Mingfei Shao

10.1002/aenm.71682.title: In Situ Formation of a Hybrid Alloy-Fluoride Interphase for Stable High-Capacity Phosphorus Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71682.abstract: ABSTRACT Phosphorus-based anodes are promising candidates for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries owing to their high theoretical capacity. However, their practical application is severely limited by drastic volume variation and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry. Achieving both mechanical robustness and rapid ion transport within the SEI remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, trace SbF 3 is doped into the phosphorus-carbon (P/C) composites through a facile ball-milling. Taking advantage of the SbF 3 preferential reduction over phosphorus, a hybrid interphase enriched with Li 3 Sb and LiF is in situ formed during initial lithiation. The hybrid interphase effectively suppresses the dissolution and shuttling of polyphosphides, which also integrates fast ionic/electronic transport with enhanced mechanical rigidity, thereby accelerating reaction kinetics. The synergetic effect endows the P/C-SbF 3 anode with a high retained capacity of 970.10 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g −1 and a superior rate capability of 893.84 mAh g −1 at 15 A g −1 . When paired with an NCM811 cathode, the full cell retains 80.25% of its capacity after 400 cycles at 1 C. The single-layer pouch full cell further confirms the practical feasibility. This work highlights in situ formed hybrid interphase engineering for overcoming the stability-transport trade-off in high-capacity alloying anodes.
authors: Gengchang Lai, Qiuyan Li, Xiaoxiao Feng, Huijuan Ma, Chao Peng, Paul K. Chu, Xue-Feng Yu, Jiahong Wang

10.1002/aenm.71684.title: Janus Ag Nanoskin-Armored Polyimide Bilayer Separator Enables Efficient Li-Nucleation Regulation for Dendrite-Free Lithium Metal Battery
10.1002/aenm.71684.abstract: ABSTRACT Uncontrolled lithium (Li) dendrite growth has been regarded as the most critical obstacle for the widespread adoption of Li metal batteries (LMBs), stemming from the preferential nucleation of Li ions (Li + ) at low-energy-barrier sites that trigger heterogeneous deposition. Therefore, it is pivotal yet significantly challenging to effectively control Li nucleation and deposition in LMBs. Here, we engineer a Janus Ag nanoskin-armored polyimide (Ag@PI/PI) bilayer separator by in situ growth Ag nanoparticles on the surface of PI nanofiber and integrating a high-strength PI nanofiber membrane as the dorsal substrate. Specifically, the Ag nanoskin acts as a three-dimensional lithiophilic host to seize Li and induce sequential Li nucleation, thereby preventing Li dendrite formation. As a result, the Ag@PI/PI-Li||Cu cell exhibits a low overpotential of 31.0 mV, high Coulombic efficiency of 98.9%, and prolonged Sand's time of 26.3 h. Significantly, the Ag@PI/PI separator delivers a high Li + transference number (0.70) and exceptional cycling stability (1600 h) in a Li||Li cell. Moreover, the Ag@PI/PI-based Li||NCM523 cell achieves a remarkable specific capacity of 108.32 mAh g −1 at 5 C while retaining a satisfying capacity retention of 88.7% at 1 C. These results underscore the viability of this universal and efficient Ag nanoskin-armored strategy for high-security LMBs applications.
authors: Pengpeng Li, Xinluo Li, Qingsong Zhang, Yisong Zhou, Junyi Han, Nianyu Yue, Jiameng Li, Jiaji Yue, Guohua Sun, Nanjun Chen

10.1002/aenm.71678.title: Medium-Concentration Electrolytes Balance Hydrogen-Bond Disruption and Ion-Ion Interactions for Wide-Temperature Aqueous Trivalent Indium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71678.abstract: ABSTRACT It is desirable to develop aqueous batteries that can operate efficiently across wide temperature ranges; however, it remains a grand challenge to simultaneously suppress electrolyte freezing at low temperatures and water-induced side reactions at elevated temperatures. Herein, we demonstrate that a medium-concentration chloride electrolyte can effectively regulate the electrolyte solvation structures, leading to high-efficiency and wide-temperature aqueous trivalent indium metal batteries. Specifically, the increment of salt concentration progressively disrupts the hydrogen-bonding network of water and reconstructs the In 3+ solvation structure toward chloride-rich complexes, achieving a balanced effect at the medium concentration (10 m) of the studied range (5, 10, and 15 m). The optimized 1 m InCl 3 + 10 m LiCl electrolyte shows the best anti-freezing property at −70°C with sufficient ionic conductivity of 1.42 mS cm −1 , and it further mitigates the In 3+ hydrolysis tendency and water-related side reactions at elevated temperatures (+65°C). Consequently, in metal anode exhibits a highly reversible plating behavior with high Coulombic efficiencies of 99%-99.95% over a wide temperature range from −70 to +65°C. Rather than simply maximizing the electrolyte concentration, our work demonstrates that balancing hydrogen-bond disruption and chloride-rich ion coordination is the key to achieving wide-temperature stability in aqueous trivalent electrolytes.
