Furthermore, a cantilever energy harvester utilizing this textured ceramic delivers an outstanding power density of 0.72 µW·mm −3 , which is 78 times higher than that of commercial soft PZT. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high-FOM piezoelectric materials for high performance energy harvesting applications.

10.1002/aenm.71521.title: Redox-Buffering PEAI-CeO x Passivation Suppresses Thermo-Mechanical Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells Under Rapid Thermal Cycling (Adv. Energy Mater. 38/2026)

10.1002/aenm.71520.title: Dual-Diol Synergized Electrolyte for Wide-Temperature Hydrogel Zn-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71520.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) feature low cost, superior safety, and eco-friendliness, promising extensive prospects for next-generation electrochemical energy storage. Nevertheless, inferior interfacial stability, uncontrollable Zn dendrite formation, and poor temperature tolerance severely hinder their practical exploitation in flexible electronic devices. Herein, glycerol (Gly) and ethylene glycol (EG) are incorporated into a polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogel matrix via a facile one-pot route to fabricate a wide-temperature-tolerant PAM-based composite hydrogel electrolyte (PAM/Gly/EG). Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two diols, the hydroxyl-rich structure reconstructs the intrinsic hydrogen bond network of confined water, while coordination interactions modulate the solvation configuration of Zn 2+ , thereby fundamentally restraining Zn dendrite propagation and parasitic hydrogen evolution. The resultant Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers a long stable lifespan over 3000 h at 1 mA·cm −2 , and sustains steady cycling for 500 h at −20°C and 300 h at 50°C. This synergistic diol modification strategy affords a feasible avenue for structural optimization and practical deployment of wide-temperature flexible AZIBs.

10.1002/aenm.71540.title: Strain Engineering in High-Entropy Electrocatalysts: Mechanisms, Strategies and Water Splitting Applications
10.1002/aenm.71540.abstract: ABSTRACT Strain engineering has emerged as an effective strategy for tailoring the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of materials at the atomic scale. For electrochemical water splitting, the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction are largely limited by scaling relationships and nonoptimized adsorption energetics of key intermediates. High-entropy materials, featuring multiprincipal-element compositions and pronounced lattice distortion, offer a unique platform for strain-mediated catalytic regulation. Their intrinsic microstrain fields, derived from atomic size mismatch together with sluggish diffusion and cocktail effects, enable tunable electronic structures and abundant metastable active sites. This review summarizes recent advances in strain engineering of high-entropy materials for water splitting. Fundamental concepts of strain and its influence on d-band centers, adsorption energetics, and reaction kinetics are first introduced. This is followed by a discussion of strain modulation strategies, including doping, solid solution alloying, and defect engineering. Special emphasis is placed on the distinct behavior of high-entropy materials compared with conventional alloys, particularly their nonlinear electronic hybridization and multisite synergy. Finally, key challenges involving strain quantification, operando evolution, and strain-entropy coupling are highlighted, providing guidance for the rational design of next-generation water-splitting catalysts.

10.1002/aenm.71531.title: Experimentally Determined Spatiotemporal Charge Carrier Dynamics for the Development of Particulate Photocatalysts
10.1002/aenm.71531.abstract: ABSTRACT Particulate photocatalysts have generated interest for the low-cost implementation of various photocatalytic processes, including the production of solar fuels as clean energy sources. With light absorption, charge generation, charge transport, and interfacial charge transfer all constrained in individual particles, complex photophysical and photochemical processes occur on a wide range of timescales within spatially defined volumes. The allure of deciphering the charge carrier dynamics to build a fundamental picture of photocatalysis in different materials has motivated the development of state-of-the-art spatiotemporal measurement techniques. Monitoring charge carrier dynamics on relevant time and length scales is a challenging experimental task. Many experimental barriers have been overcome in recent years, providing some guidance for future directions for material development. This review delves into the underlying origins of spatial heterogeneity in charge carrier dynamics, introduces charge carrier transport phenomena, and details the recent examples of spatiotemporal investigation of charge carrier dynamics in particulate photocatalysts. These new experimental capabilities pave the way for a more comprehensive description of photocatalytic processes, guiding the optimization of photocatalytic materials.

10.1002/aenm.71552.title: Holistic Top-to-Bottom Film Restructuring to Achieve Highly Stable Unencapsulated Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71552.abstract: ABSTRACT While perovskites have emerged as frontrunners in optoelectronics due to their exceptional properties, their performance remains bottlenecked by film imperfections such as interfacial defects, non-uniform crystallization, and band alignment mismatches. Conventional treatments often fail to simultaneously address issues at the top surface, the bulk, and the buried interface. In this work, we introduce a holistic top-to-bottom restructuring strategy using a facile vapor-phase post-treatment. This approach induces a gradient-distributed 2D perovskite phase that extends from the surface into the bulk while uniquely healing structural voids and chemical inhomogeneities at the buried interface. This synergistic restructuring optimizes the energy band structure for accelerated carrier extraction and passivates defects throughout the entire film depth. As a result, our unencapsulated n-i-p solar cells demonstrate exceptional environmental resilience, maintaining over 90% of their initial efficiency after 2,800 h of high-humidity exposure. This study establishes a new benchmark for stability and provides a robust pathway for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

10.1002/aenm.71535.title: Elucidating the Suppression of High-Voltage Degradation in O3-type NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 : A Voltage-Switching Strategy for Na-ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71535.abstract: ABSTRACT Elevating depth-of-charge (DoC) enhances the energy density of layered oxide cathodes for sodium-ion batteries; however, such high-DoC cycling inevitably triggers severe structural and interfacial degradation. In practice, battery management systems commonly adapt voltage-derating strategies dynamically according to battery state of health, achieving a favorable trade-off between energy density and cycle life. Nevertheless, a critical yet overlooked question remains: how high-DoC-induced damaged regions evolve when reverted to moderate-DoC cycling. Here, using NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM111) as a prototype, a voltage-switching strategy is employed to elucidate the dynamic and long-term behavior of these damaged regions. During high-DoC cycling (charging to 4.3 V), the rapid capacity fading is driven by pronounced formation of bulk defects and interfacial disordered spinel phases. However, upon switching these cells to moderate-DoC cycling (charging to 4.0 V), these pre-existing damaged regions become stabilized: their rapid propagation is suppressed, and they no longer accelerate degradation in surrounding intact regions. This enables degraded NFM111 to deliver capacity retention comparable to that of cells cycled solely under moderate-DoC conditions. This work presents a dynamic and evolving picture of high-DoC degradation and subsequent moderate-DoC stabilization in NFM111 cathodes, providing mechanistic insights into voltage-derating process and the lifetime prolongation of compromised cells.

10.1002/aenm.71515.title: Volatilization-Kinetics-Dictated Crystallization Enabling Efficient Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells for Near-Space Environment
10.1002/aenm.71515.abstract: ABSTRACT The remarkable progress in metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has propelled perovskite/silicon tandem architectures as a transformative solution in photovoltaics, enabling efficiencies beyond single-junction limits while offering high specific power and radiation resistance for challenging environments, including near-space and aerospace applications. Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites on textured silicon, however, encounter hurdles in controlled crystallization and halide phase stability, leading to recombination losses and reduced performance. This work investigates additive engineering using volatile alkylammonium chlorides with tailored alkyl chain lengths to fine-tune volatilization kinetics. By strategically slowing down the volatilization rate, the additive promotes homogeneous nucleation and retards grain growth, which is critical for achieving uniform perovskite coverage over the intricate topography of textured silicon substrates.​ An optimized additive promotes dense, oriented films with suppressed segregation, culminating in tandem solar cells boasting a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 31.1% and stability exceeding 1000 h. First-ever flight test measurements and calibrations of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells were conducted under near-space conditions at altitudes reaching 37.29 km. These advancements may contribute to the development of robust tandem devices for various application settings.

10.1002/aenm.71514.title: Clean Tin Oxide via Volatile Additive Engineering for High-performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/aenm.71514.abstract: ABSTRACT SnO 2 is a benchmark electron transport material for perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, SnO 2 films from the conventional chemical bath deposition (CBD) are limited by impurities and defects that accelerate non-radiative recombination and compromise device stability. Here, we present a volatile additive engineering strategy using pyruvic acid (PA) as a dual-functional nucleation promoter and surface modulator during SnO 2 deposition. Owing to its volatility (sublimation at 145°C), PA can be effectively removed during annealing, resulting in cleaner SnO 2 surfaces with reduced residual groups. This is accompanied by a decrease in oxygen-related defect densities in the SnO 2 layer. This improvement leads to enhanced charge recombination and improved thermal stability at the buried interface. Consequently, PA-engineered PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.17%, together with improved device stability, retaining >80% of their initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation, 1000 h at 65°C, and 30 days under 30% relative humidity. Furthermore, this approach is compatible with large-area fabrication, yielding efficiencies of 24.83% for 1 cm 2 lab-scale cells and 20.21% for 30 cm × 30 cm industrial-scale solar modules. These results suggest that controlling additive volatility improves CBD-SnO 2 quality and offers a promising route for stable, scalable perovskite solar cells.

10.1002/aenm.71533.title: Enabling Low-Temperature Fast-Charging Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries: A Synergistic Design of Electrolyte Solvation and Current Collector Interface
10.1002/aenm.71533.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) promise ultrahigh energy density (>350 Wh kg −1 ) and low cost, yet their operation under low-temperature and fast-charging conditions is critically hindered by limited sodium inventory and sluggish interfacial kinetics. This conflict creates a “stability paradox”: the pursuit of high energy density amplifies interfacial instability, leading to inhomogeneous sodium deposition and rapid capacity decay. This review systematically analyzes AFSMB failure mechanisms under extreme conditions and demonstrates that overcoming these bottlenecks requires integrated co-design across four synergistic domains: (1) engineering electrolyte solvation structures (weakly solvating, high-concentration, and high-entropy designs) to lower the desolvation barrier and stabilize the solid-electrolyte interphase; (2) tailoring current collector interfaces with sodiophilic coatings or three-dimensional architectures to guide uniform sodium deposition; (3) incorporating rational pre-sodiation strategies to compensate irreversible sodium loss; and (4) leveraging artificial intelligence and molecular simulations for data-driven electrolyte screening. We critically assess the trade-offs of each strategy and provide a forward-looking perspective on reversible sodium compensation, multi-scale AI platforms, and full-cell integration. This review offers a roadmap for developing practical, wide-temperature-range, high-energy-density AFSMBs, with recent pouch cells already demonstrating >200 Wh kg −1 and stable cycling from −40°C to 60°C.

10.1002/aenm.71530.title: Redox-Mediated Electrified Method for Green and Low-Cost Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Materials Recycling
10.1002/aenm.71530.abstract: ABSTRACT After 30 years of commercialization and mass production, lithium-ion batteries have generated massive waste streams, especially with their expanding use in electric vehicles. Recycling spent batteries and valorizing useful components are therefore increasingly urgent for sustainable development. However, conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical methods are limited by high energy consumption or large chemical input, creating demand for greener and more efficient recycling technologies. Here, using LiCoO 2 as an example, we report a closed-loop electrified chemical process based on redox-targeting reactions to recover valuable species from spent battery materials using only electricity and water. Complementary reductive leaching of LiCoO 2 and oxidative leaching of LiFePO 4 were performed with anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonate as a regenerative redox mediator to sequentially break down LiCoO 2 and achieve efficient separation of Co 2+ and Li + in the form of Co(OH) 2 and LiOH. This cost-effective and environmentally friendly method was also extended to the recycling of LiNi x Mn y Co z O 2 with a high recovery rate of Li + and transition metal species. It is anticipated that the electrified chemical recycling method demonstrated here would provide a credible solution to the valorization of battery waste and contribute to the sustainable development of lithium-ion batteries.

10.1002/aenm.71534.title: Chelation Compensation Strategy for High-Performance Iron-Based Redox Flow Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71534.abstract: ABSTRACT Iron-based redox flow batteries (IRFBs) are compelling candidates for cost-effective grid-scale energy storage, benefiting from high safety, low cost, and the natural abundance of iron-based active species. However, heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and kinetic deactivation lead to capacity decay and energy efficiency reduction, which limits the long-term cycle stability of IRFBs. Chelation compensation is employed to regulate metal-ion redox species through multidentate ligand design. Their coordination environment, solvation structure, and interfacial reactivity are thereby optimized, leading to improved energy efficiency and cycling stability. This review summarizes the major degradation mechanisms of IRFBs and highlights recent progress in chelation-modified systems constructed with representative chelating functional groups. Particular attention is given to the influence of chelation on heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and reaction kinetics. Finally, current challenges and future directions in ligand design, electrolyte compatibility, mechanistic understanding, and practical implementation are discussed, offering guidance for the development of high-performance chelation-modified IRFBs for large-scale energy storage.

10.1002/aenm.71537.title: Integrating Machine Learning and High-Throughput Calculations for the Rational Design of Photocatalytic 2D-COFs on Overall Water Splitting
10.1002/aenm.71537.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D-COFs) with tunable structures offer a promising platform for photocatalytic overall water splitting (OWS) under visible-light. However, it is challenging to quickly find photocatalytic OWS materials from the massive amounts of 2D-COFs and then achieve precise synthesis. In this work, we constructed 11 934 hcb-type 2D-COFs by assembling 28 building blocks and 9 linkages. The machine learning (ML) and high-throughput computation (HTC) were integrated to predict feasible photocatalytic OWS hcb-type 2D-COFs. Through training 10 initial algorithms and optimizing the hyperparameters of top 4 algorithms in terms of performance, the ETR model for predicting the band-edge levels with R 2 of 0.97 and 0.99 was developed, and the KNR and RFR models were built for predicting Δ G *H and Δ G *OH with R 2 of 0.99 and 0.83, respectively. 2581 2D-COFs (21.63% of dataset) are screened to be potential structures for visible-light-driven water splitting. After applying the optimal ML models on all assembled 2D-COFs, a list of high-frequency building blocks and linkages is suggested as a set of suitable candidates for the first time. Then TBTZ_FBN0_Imine (TBTZ-FBN0-COF) was assembled and experimentally synthesized. Its OWS activity verified our ML-HTC paradigm, which provides the researchers recommendation to construct photocatalytic OWS 2D-COFs.

10.1002/aenm.71551.title: Interface Engineering via Ceria Coating Reconciles Ion Transport and Lithium Compatibility in Composite Polymer Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71551.abstract: ABSTRACT Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) exhibit considerable potential for solid−state lithium−metal batteries (SLBs). However, incompatibilities between the various components in the electrolyte continue to hinder the full realization of its performance and practical applications. In this work, a multifunctional ceria interfacial layer is proposed to achieve uniform dispersion of ceramic fillers and facilitated interfacial transport of lithium ions in CPEs. At the same time, the physical barrier provided by this multifunctional interface layer prevents direct contact between the ceramic filler and the lithium metal, thereby avoiding potentially harmful side reactions that could further lead to a performance deterioration in battery cycling. Owing to the introduction of this multifunctional interface layer, the CPE exhibits high ionic conductivity (0.772 mS cm −1 ) and Li-ion transference number (0.626), with a wide electrochemical window (5.03 V). Furthermore, the Li|CPE|Li symmetric cell exhibits a lithium deposition/stripping capacity exceeding 1500 h at room temperature, indicating the CPE's excellent ability to suppress interfacial side reactions. Li|CPE|NCM811 cells retained a capacity of 77% after 350 cycles, whilst pouch cells retained 76% after 300 stable cycles at room temperature and 0.5 C. The method of optimizing ceramic fillers offers new insights into the design of novel composite solid-state electrolytes for SLBs.

10.1002/aenm.71532.title: Unraveling Spatial Electrochemical Heterogeneity and Additive-Mediated Regulation in Scale-up Aqueous Zinc-Ion Pouch-Type Cells
10.1002/aenm.71532.abstract: ABSTRACT Scaling aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) to pouch-type configurations amplifies electric-field and Zn 2+ flux heterogeneities, causing non-uniform Zn deposition. Here, β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and Tween 80 (Tw80) are systematically investigated to decouple bulk transport and interfacial kinetic regulation in scale-up pouch-type cells. β-CD increases ionic conductivity (3.44 to 5.95 mS cm − 1 ) and the Zn 2+ transference number (0.16 to 0.47), promoting uniform bulk ion flux and extending symmetric pouch-type cell lifespan beyond 1000 h at 1 mA cm − 2 . Conversely, Tw80 operates via interfacial adsorption to regulate local reaction kinetics, achieving stable cycling for >600 h. Spatially resolved analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and in situ thermal imaging reveal that β-CD suppresses macroscopic heterogeneity across near-tab, central, and edge regions by stabilizing bulk solvation, whereas Tw80 mitigates localized interfacial instability. In practical Zn||V 2 O 5 pouch-type full cells, β-CD delivers superior long-term capacity retention, while Tw80 excels under high-rate conditions. This work identifies spatial electrochemical heterogeneity as a primary scaling limit and offers general design principles connecting additive chemistry, transport kinetics, and format-dependent deposition for practical AZIBs.

10.1002/aenm.71516.title: Highly Efficient and Cost-Effective Single-Atom Catalysts for Lithium-Sulfur Batteries Exceeding 540 Wh kg −1
10.1002/aenm.71516.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the high theoretical energy density (2600 Wh kg −1 ) of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, their practical application in low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles is severely hindered by sluggish reaction kinetics and the severe shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides, making it difficult to meet the stringent demands for high-rate capability and high energy density. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a promising strategy to accelerate polysulfide conversion kinetics. However, conventional SACs often face challenges such as high preparation costs, complex synthetic processes, and catalyst poisoning due to excessively strong binding with sulfur species. To address these technical and economic limitations, this work focuses on developing cost-effective and efficient materials for large-scale energy storage. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ), a low-cost, easily scalable material with abundant nitrogen coordination sites, was selected as the substrate to prepare an atomically dispersed SAC (Mn-CN). Benefiting from the unique half-filled 3d electronic configuration of the Mn atom, the catalyst directly establishes a robust “Mn-S and Li-N” dual-coordination mechanism. This specific interaction effectively activates the Li─S bond and substantially lowers the thermodynamic energy barriers, thereby improving the redox kinetics of polysulfide conversion. Consequently, the assembled Li-S batteries maintain a reversible capacity of 658 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 4 C and exhibit stable long cycling performance. Furthermore, the assembled 14 Ah-level pouch cell achieves an initial energy density of 547 Wh kg −1 and over 30 stable cycles. This work provides a practical approach for preparing cost-effective and efficient single-atom catalysts, supporting the industrial application of high-energy-density Li-S batteries.

10.1002/aenm.71341.title: Non-Bonding Element Doping Enables Weakened Electron-Phonon Interaction and Superior Thermoelectric Performance in CuGaTe 2
10.1002/aenm.71341.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional thermoelectric materials suffer from a fundamental trade-off between carrier concentration and mobility ascribed to the Coulomb scattering from ionized impurities under heavy doping. Here, we demonstrate a novel non-bonding doping mechanism in Mg-doped CuGaTe 2 with barely affected carrier mobility. Ultrafast dynamics analysis reveals a substantially reduced carrier scattering potential in Mg-doped CuGaTe 2 compared to that doped by other dopants. First-principles calculations show that Mg with only active s electrons, neither has bonding nor antibonding states with the orbitals of Te in the vicinity of valence band edge. Such unique non-bonding character weakens the dependence of energy level on lattice deformation, resulting in suppressed electron-phonon interactions. Consequently, the carrier mobility is enhanced by ∼100%, leading to a high average power factor of 1.66 mW m −1 K −2 . Further alloying Cu with Ag to reduce lattice thermal conductivity leads to a record-high peak zT of 2.1 at 973 K and the highest reported average zT of 0.93 over 294-973 K. Our findings underscore the critical role of dopant orbital hybridization in tailoring electron-phonon interactions, providing a rational doping strategy for high-performance thermoelectric materials and other electronic materials that require high carrier mobility.

10.1002/aenm.71380.title: Breaking the Polarity-Coordination Coupling in Electrolyte Design for High-Voltage Lithium Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71380.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte design is fundamentally constrained by the trade-off between high solvent polarity and weak Li + solvation, as polar solvents typically bind Li + strongly. Here, we establish a steric-electronic modulation strategy that decouples solvent polarity from Li + coordination, enabling a generalizable pseudo-weak solvation electrolyte design paradigm. Based on this principle, a steric hindrance-mediated electrolyte is developed combining 2,2,2-trifluoro-N, N-dimethylethylamide (DMTFA) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) with dual lithium salts. Despite its strong polarity, DMTFA exhibits weak Li + coordination due to the combined steric hindrance and electron-withdrawing effects of the -CF 3 group, enabling anion- dominated solvation structures. This coordination chemistry lowers Li + desolvation barriers and drives the preferential adsorption of a B- and P-rich interphase layer at the cathode surface, thereby protecting the cathode from HF corrosion. The resulting electrolyte achieves high ionic conductivity, intrinsic flame retardancy, and an electrochemical stability window exceeding 5.0 V. Cells employing LiNi 0.91 Co 0.06 Mn 0.03 O 2 cathodes demonstrate a capacity retention of over 90.0% after 100 cycles at 1 C rate and 4.8 V charge cut-off. The electrolyte enables approximately 1.6 Ah pouch cells to retain 84.97% capacity after 1800 cycles at 4.6 V.

10.1002/adfm.78905.title: Nitrospinics: Nitride Materials for Spin-Orbit and Orbital Torques From Memory to Artificial Intelligence
10.1002/adfm.78905.abstract: ABSTRACT The exploration of energy-efficient and functional spintronics has attracted considerable attention. Spin-orbit and orbital transport have opened new pathways for current-induced torque generation based on the spin Hall effect. In addition, artificial intelligence computing has been demonstrated using spintronic devices. Further progress of these devices can be anticipated through the development of unique and functional materials, beyond the existing heavy metals and topological systems with strong spin-orbit coupling. The nitride materials exhibit unique chemical, magnetic, and structural versatility, including antiferromagnetism, high thermal stability, and compatibility with diverse device architectures. Here, we propose Nitrospinics as a conceptual and functional framework that exploits nitride materials for applications ranging from spin-orbit and orbital torque based spintronic devices to artificial intelligence hardware. Using a sputter-grown multilayer Cr 2 N with MXene-related layer structure and a nitrogen-incorporated heavy metal of Pt x N, as prototype systems, we discuss how nitrogen contributes to the structural stability, the orbital torque and spin-orbit torque generation, and the interfacial orbital to spin conversion. We further outline key challenges and opportunities toward establishing nitride-based materials for next-generation computing technologies.

10.1002/adfm.78438.title: Optimizing NiMo Electrocatalyst Coatings for Hydrogen Evolution in Alkaline Electrolysis With The Machine Learning-Guided Autonomous Platform CatBot
10.1002/adfm.78438.abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of efficient, durable, and platinum group metal-free electrocatalysts for alkaline water electrolysis is essential to reduce the cost of green hydrogen. Efficient exploration of the vast possible synthetic space is nevertheless hindered by the slow pace of manual experimentation. Here, a closed-loop optimization is presented that combines an automated electrocatalyst synthesis and testing system, CatBot, with Bayesian optimization and accelerated stress testing at industrial conditions for the rapid discovery of active and durable NiMo coatings. Distinct regions with exceptionally high activity and stability are identified within limited experimental budgets on a nickel wire substrate, using different search strategies to efficiently navigate the six-dimensional synthesis space exceeding possible combinations. The most promising coatings are upscaled onto technological nickel foam electrodes showing platinum-level catalytic activity with overpotentials of 173 mV at -1 in 30 wt.% KOH at for the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the autonomous optimization of functional electrocatalyst coatings under realistic operating conditions.

10.1002/adfm.78942.title: Optical Responses of Topological and Plasmonic Heterostructures for Photothermal and Photocatalytic Applications
10.1002/adfm.78942.abstract: ABSTRACT Topological materials represent unique solids characterized by the global invariance of their bulk electronic band structure. Owing to their distinctive properties, such as ultra-high electron mobility, spin-momentum locking, and the presence of massless Dirac fermions, topological materials provide a promising platform for applications in electronics, spintronics, and energy conversion. By integrating topological materials with other functional systems, it is possible to harness the advantages of topologically protected surface states along with other versatile properties, thereby enabling novel optical behaviors for photo-driven applications. In this review, we provide a concise overview of recent advances in the rational design and optical responses of topological and plasmonic heterostructures, emphasizing their unique advantages and potential in photothermal and photocatalytic applications. We begin by examining the fundamental principles and optical characteristics of topological materials, as well as the underlying mechanisms responsible for their enhanced photothermal and catalytic performance. Subsequently, we review recent progress in the chemical and physical preparation of both two-component and three-component topological-plasmonic heterostructures, along with their resulting optical responses. Finally, we highlight significant recent developments in the use of topological and plasmonic heterostructures for photothermal and photocatalytic applications and offer a brief perspective on current challenges and future research directions.

10.1002/adfm.79003.title: Angular-Multiplexed Photoluminescence Meta-Display via Unidirectional Emission Control
10.1002/adfm.79003.abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurfaces have revolutionized the optical field due to their exceptional wavefront shaping capabilities, boosting the multi-dimensional light-field manipulation and emission control. However, the incoherent, omnidirectional, unpolarized, and phase-random nature of fluorescence emission limits the applicability of conventional metasurface multiplexing strategies, posing significant challenges for photoluminescence (PL) encoding and multi-dimensional light-emitting metasurface (LEM)-based display technology. Here, the PL angular-multiplexing is proposed and experimentally demonstrated based on unidirectional emission control for multi-dimensional meta-display. By exploiting the inherent numerical aperture limitation of the detection system and coupling PL into the guided mode via an on-chip metasurface, the LEM-empowered precise emission angle control is transferred into the angular-multiplexed intensity encoding degree of freedom, enabling a dual-channel PL meta-display. Furthermore, by incorporating directional multiplexing, the multi-dimensional LEM achieves four independent PL images corresponding to distinct observation angles and illumination directions. This PL angular-multiplexing approach, together with the multi-dimensional meta-display architecture, significantly expands the multiplexing encoding capability of fluorescence light-field manipulation, offering promising opportunities for diverse applications, including next-generation optical display/encryption techniques, biological sensing, and incoherent illumination engineering.

10.1002/adfm.79026.title: Large Language Model Directed Iteration for the Design of Ultra-Stable Sodium-Ion Battery
10.1002/adfm.79026.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into materials discovery is hindered by the trade-off between exploration breadth and exploitation depth, while the lack of embedded domain knowledge and systematic chemical space compression further limits intelligent materials exploration under data scarcity. Herein, we propose a literature-knowledge-directed iterative workflow that combines large language models (LLMs) with Bayesian optimization (BO) for the rational electrolyte design for ultra-stable sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). LLMs serve as auxiliary tools for knowledge mining, while BO accelerates multi-objective optimization to obtain electrolyte compositions. The optimized dual-anion hybrid solvation electrolyte (DHSE) constructs a synergistic solvation structure, which induces the formation of a compact, inorganic-rich, and mechanically robust cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). The as-formed CEI layer suppresses parasitic side reactions and accelerates Na + transport by reducing the desolvation barrier. Remarkably, industrial-scale Ah-level hard carbon||NaNi 0.3 Mn 0.3 Fe 0.3 O 2 pouch cells assembled with DHSE deliver a high energy density of 107.7 Wh kg −1 , alongside a superior capacity retention of 94% after 100 cycles at 0.5C. This work not only develops a high-performance electrolyte for practically applicable SIBs but also provides a general human-agent collaborative framework for intelligent materials development under data-limited conditions.

10.1002/adfm.78975.title: Carbon Dot-Engineered Dual-Action Exosomes Rescue Mitochondrial Homeostasis by Intercepting RIRR and Activating PGC-1α in Severe Ischemia
10.1002/adfm.78975.abstract: ABSTRACT Severe ischemic diseases are driven by oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles (M2-EVs) offer substantial regenerative potential, yet their clinical translation is hindered by microenvironmental degradation and a lack of targeting. We developed an engineered bio-nano hybrid platform (M2-EVs@CDs-TPP) by integrating triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-functionalized carbon dots (CDs) with M2-EVs. This design enables a dual-localization mode, wherein CDs-TPP act as an antioxidant shield on the vesicle surface to enhance cellular uptake, while also serving as a subcellular navigator to precisely direct the therapeutic payload to damaged mitochondria. Mechanistically, the system exerts a dual-action therapeutic effect. It chemically scavenges pathogenic mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) to disrupt the ROS-induced ROS release (RIRR) cycle. Concurrently, this relief of oxidative stress synergizes with M2-EVs to activate the Nrf2-PGC-1α metabolic regulatory hub. This biological reprogramming establishes robust biphasic antioxidant defenses (via HO-1 and SOD2) and drives mitochondrial biogenesis (via NRF1/TFAM), reestablishing cellular ATP homeostasis. In vitro and in a murine critical limb ischemia model, this metabolic rewiring drove multidimensional tissue regeneration, encompassing angiogenesis, myoblast differentiation, and anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization. This work provides a modular engineering strategy to overcome translational barriers of native EVs and highlights the clinical potential of targeting mitochondrial metabolism for pan-ischemic disease therapy.

10.1002/adfm.78795.title: FAK-Targeting Microneedle Patch Promotes Uterine Regenerative Repair and Restores Reproductive Function Post-Cesarean Section Via Inhibiting Mechanotransduction
10.1002/adfm.78795.abstract: ABSTRACT Uterine scarring after cesarean section is a major cause of secondary infertility and uterine rupture, and its formation is closely associated with disruption of the mechanical microenvironment at incision sites, yet its mechanobiological basis and effective mechano-regulatory therapies remain poorly defined. We identify focal adhesion kinase (FAK)-mediated mechanotransduction as a key driver of post-cesarean uterine scar formation. To target this process, we developed FAK-PTC-Lipo@MN, a biodegradable microneedle patch composed of gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) and ε-poly-L-lysine-glycidyl methacrylate (EPLGMA), enabling sustained local delivery of FAK-PROTAC-loaded liposomes. In a rat cesarean-section model, FAK-PTC-Lipo@MN reduced inflammatory infiltration, collagen deposition, myometrial thickening, and tissue stiffness, thereby suppressing uterine scar formation. Transcriptomic analysis further showed a shift of uterine repair mode from fibrotic toward regenerative repair, with activation of Wnt/Notch-related pathways and downregulation of ECM-associated fibrotic signaling. Functionally, FAK-PTC-Lipo@MN promoted uterine functional recovery and improved key reproductive outcomes (e.g., conception time, fetal number, and fetal weight) after cesarean section. Mechanistically, released FAK-PTC-Lipo induced FAK degradation and inhibited its activation, thereby reducing F-actin polymerization, cell traction forces, ECM remodeling and tension, and N-cadherin-dependent fibroblast collective migration. This study establishes FAK-targeted mechanotherapy as a promising strategy for uterine incision regeneration and reproductive function restoration after cesarean section.

10.1002/adfm.78969.title: Spatially Progressive Penetration Self-Propelled Nanomotors for Stepwise Eradication of Biofilm and Deep-Tissue-Infected Wounds Remodeling
10.1002/adfm.78969.abstract: ABSTRACT Current therapies for chronic infected wounds primarily rely on multifunctional nanoplatforms with antibacterial, anti-biofilm, and anti-inflammatory properties. However, biofilms are often overlooked as the initial physical barrier that must be disrupted before therapeutic agents can effectively penetrate deep inflammatory tissues and eliminate residual infection. In addition, heterogeneous infection microenvironments demand versatile therapeutic systems. To address these challenges, this study developed self-propelled nanomotors (Dex@CQDs@mPDA) and proposed a spatially progressive penetration strategy to achieve precise, stepwise treatment from the surface to deep tissues. First, dextran (Dex) surface modification enables targeted recognition of bacterial biofilms, while the near-infrared (NIR) photothermal effect facilitates biofilm disruption. Subsequently, mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA) catalyzes H 2 O 2 to generate O 2 , which, together with carbon quantum dots (CQDs)-mediated NO release, produces a dual-gas-driven propulsion effect, promoting active penetration into deep inflammatory tissues. Meanwhile, the nanomotors effectively scavenge excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), promote macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, enhance angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and remodel the inflammatory microenvironment to accelerate tissue regeneration. In vitro experiments further confirmed their excellent antibacterial, antibiofilm, and anti-inflammatory activities, as well as their broad applicability across diverse infection scenarios. This work provides a therapeutic strategy that links biofilm eradication with deep inflammation resolution.

10.1002/adfm.78959.title: Oral Butyrate-Functionalized Magnetic Nanorobots for Targeted Exosome Transport in the Theranostics of Early-Stage Colorectal Cancer
10.1002/adfm.78959.abstract: ABSTRACT Early detection and intervention are critical to reducing colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality. Although tumor-derived exosomes (TDEs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, their extremely low abundance in peripheral blood during early carcinogenesis severely limits clinical utility for early diagnosis. Here, we report a theranostic magnetic nanorobot (MNP-BC), comprising Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 nanoparticles co-functionalized with butyrate and anti-CD147 antibody. Oral administration followed by magnetic guidance, MNP-BC accumulates at colonic tumor sites, where butyrate selectively induces cancer cell apoptosis, boosts CD8 + T-cell cytotoxicity, and preserves intestinal barrier integrity. Concurrently, the anti-CD147 antibody moiety captures TDEs in situ. Following monocarboxylate transporter-mediated uptake, intracellular butyrate metabolism releases the MNP-TDEs complex into circulation, thereby enriching plasma TDEs for magnetic isolation and noninvasive detection. In early-stage CRC mice, MNP-BC markedly suppressed tumor progression and facilitated sensitive diagnosis via TDEs signal amplification. This work introduces an integrated “TDEs signal amplification-sensitive diagnosis-in situ therapy” platform, offering a rationally engineered strategy to address key translational barriers in early CRC detection and intervention.

10.1002/adfm.78996.title: Phase-Pure 2D/3D Perovskite Heterojunctions Enabled by n -Specific Nanocrystal Templates for High-Efficiency and Stable Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78996.abstract: ABSTRACT Tailoring phase purity in 2D/3D perovskites is essential for balanced charge transport and long-term stability. Here, we develop a nanocrystal-templated epitaxial strategy to construct phase-pure 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions. Phase-pure 2D perovskite nanocrystals with tunable quantum-well thickness ( n = 1-4) are used as templates to direct lattice-matched epitaxial growth of 3D perovskites, yielding coherent 2D/3D interfaces. By precisely controlling the 2D quantum-well thickness, we eliminate the phase-mixing issues of conventional methods and ensure high interfacial phase purity. A series of well-defined 2D/3D heterojunctions ( n = 1-4) exhibits balanced charge transport and markedly reduced recombination losses. The optimized 2D ( n = 4)/3D perovskite solar cell delivers a power conversion efficiency of 26.48% and retains over 90% of its initial performance after 1 600 h, demonstrating enhanced efficiency and long-term stability. Our work provides a versatile route for constructing phase-pure 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions, enabling optoelectronic devices with balanced charge transport and long-term stability.

10.1002/adfm.78974.title: X-QZS Metamaterial: A Novel Mechanical Metamaterial of Morphological Nonlinearity via Topological Transformations
10.1002/adfm.78974.abstract: ABSTRACT The key challenge for advancing next-generation mechanical metamaterials lies in systematically discovering and harnessing the beneficial nonlinear mechanical characteristics. This work introduces a novel class of mechanical metamaterials exhibiting morphological nonlinearity of mechanics in stiffness and Poisson's ratio, achieving purposeful nonlinear performance with quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) through topological transformations from X-shaped rigid-body mechanism. The proposed topology transformation miniaturizes, reshapes, and reprograms tailorable nonlinear stiffness of solid mechanism into elastic metamaterial. Governed by compliant elements and nonlinear meta-atoms, architected matrices culminate in a novel family termed as X-QZS metamaterial. Localized topology faithfully emulates the nonlinear kinematics of their rigid-body counterparts, meanwhile meta-atoms incubate tailorable nonlinear stiffness with topological morphologies. Assembled in nonlinear Poisson's ratio matrix, X-QZS matrix reprograms nonlinear stiffness from meta-atomic level into stabilized structural pattern. Experimental demonstrations validate the presence of QZS in multiple configurations as analytically determined in the topology design, achieving wide-bandwidth vibration isolation starting from 2 Hz and attenuating vibration energy from external sources by more than 98%. X-QZS metamaterial with tailorable dual nonlinearity and its topology pave the way of developing functional mechanical metamaterials transferred from rigid-body structures, which reprogram and reshape large-scale mechanisms into continuum deformable metamaterial of equivalent performance.

10.1002/adfm.78946.title: GeS as an Emerging OTS Material: Atomic Structure and Modeling of ON/OFF Switching
10.1002/adfm.78946.abstract: ABSTRACT Time-of-flight neutron and high-energy x-ray diffraction, together with Raman spectroscopy performed on tiny splat-quenched GeS droplets (2.6 mg total), supported by first-principles molecular dynamics and DFT modeling of vibrational properties, were employed to decipher the atomic and electronic structure of this promising OTS material for next-generation high-density memory architectures. A half-century-old structural controversy, between a continuous 4:2 random network of tetrahedra and a distorted trigonal model derived from orthorhombic GeS, is resolved, revealing instead a patchwork of mixed tetrahedral and trigonal units. Finite-field FPMD simulations predict that, under a high electric field driving the ON state, a mild structural transformation begins, characterized by a partial conversion of mixed tetrahedra into strongly deformed defect-octahedral units with elongated interatomic distances and a reduced population of Ge─Ge homopolar bonds. The simulations reveal that emerging under- and over-coordinated Ge and S species, accompanied by three-membered rings, form an interconnected defect network associated with overlapping, localized, and extended mid-gap states near the Fermi level and with bandgap closure. These computational results suggest that the resulting donor-like and acceptor-like centers and amphoteric defect sites enable high-rate electron hopping and tunneling, thereby generating strong electrical contrast between the low-conducting OFF and highly conductive ON states.

10.1002/adfm.78987.title: Navigating the Growth-Strain Trade-Off in 2D Perovskite Solar Cells via Surface Self-Templated Dual-Anion Synergy
10.1002/adfm.78987.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) perovskites are promising candidates for solar cells. However, the processing strategies that promote large, oriented grains often concurrently induce tensile strain and microcracks, creating a critical growth-strain trade-off. Herein, we propose a surface self-templated dual-anion synergy by partially substituting iodide with low amounts of thiocyanate and chloride (2 mol%) in 2D (AA) 2 (MA) 3 Pb 4 I 13 perovskites ( n = 4), in which SCN anion spontaneously enriches at the top surface as a structure-directing template that drives oriented grain growth but inevitably introduces tensile strain, and Cl anion concurrently segregates to the top surface as a strain buffer that alleviates this strain without sacrificing grain size. Systematic in situ and depth-resolved analysis reveals that such synergy effectively navigates the growth-strain trade-off of 2D perovskites, yielding enlarged grains, strong vertical orientation, and a crack-free morphology, which contributes to the suppression of non-radiative recombination and the enhancement of charge transport in solar cells. As a result, the champion device with dual-anion engineering achieves a remarkable efficiency of 19.11%, and retains over 95% of its initial efficiency after 1800 h under one-sun irradiation. This work establishes a fundamental understanding of the growth-strain dilemma in 2D perovskites, providing a universal design principle for high-efficiency 2D perovskite solar cells.

10.1002/adfm.78972.title: Multifunctional and Near Zero-Strain Li-Rich In-Li Intermetallic Anodes for Stable Cycling of Li-S Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78972.abstract: ABSTRACT Li-S batteries (LSBs) are emerging as formidable contenders in the field of energy storage systems, owing to their cost-effectiveness and ultrahigh energy density that surpasses that of conventional Li-ion batteries. Nonetheless, unresolved issues, such as Li dendrite growth and parasitic chemical reactions between the Li metal and dissolved polysulfides, pose significant safety concerns and remain major hurdles to their commercial viability. Herein, we propose a Li-rich In 3 Li 13 intermetallic alloy anode (In-Li IMA) fabricated via a simple roll-pressing and pressure-holding process. Unlike previous studies that focused primarily on stabilized interfaces for dendrite suppression, the in situ-formed In-Li IMA demonstrates not only significantly inhibited dendritic Li growth but also minimized volume change during cycling, owing to its ionically and electronically conductive 3D framework. Furthermore, simulation studies reveal that the In-Li IMA suppresses polysulfide-induced side reactions due to its hole-dominated conduction and weaker polysulfide adsorption energy relative to Li. In contrast to the control Li cell that exhibits significant capacity fading, the In-Li IMA cell achieves 87.4% capacity retention over 600 cycles and exhibits improved cyclability even in large-area pouch-cell configurations. Based on this accessible approach for fabricating large-scale multifunctional anodes, this study provides critical design insights for developing practical anodes for LSBs.

10.1002/adfm.78958.title: Dual-Sided Regulation of Lithium Deposition for High-Energy-Density Anode-Less Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78958.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-less lithium (Li) metal batteries are the ultimate anode configuration for high-energy-density energy storage, yet their practical adoption is hindered by uncontrolled Li dendrite growth. Here, we present a dual-sided regulation strategy that homogenizes Li deposition through simultaneous bottom-up and top-down control. At the current collector, an ultrathin platinum (Pt) layer leverages its lithiophilicity to stabilize nucleation and promote dense bottom growth. At the separator, an amorphous tantalum oxide (a-TaO x ) ceramic layer exploits thermodynamic Li dewetting to suppress upward dendritic propagation, enforcing top-down uniformity. This synergistic Pt/a-TaO x dual-interface design orchestrates Li deposition across the entire electrode, enabling stable cycling at high cathode areal capacities (4.78 mAh cm- 2 ) with 70% capacity retention after 110 cycles in an anode-less configuration (N/P ratio = 0) and 80% after 187 cycles with pre-lithiation (N/P ratio = 0.42). By transcending conventional bottom-only protection, this work establishes a new framework for stabilizing Li deposition across the full thickness in high-capacity anode-less Li metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78592.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Dopant-Class Design Enables Near-Zero-Strain P2-Type Cathodes for High-Voltage Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78592.abstract: ABSTRACT Manganese-based layered oxides are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their practical deployment is restricted by Mn 3+ -induced Jahn-Teller distortion, irreversible high-voltage P2-O2 phase transitions, and oxygen-related side reactions that collectively cause structural deterioration and rapid capacity fading. Here, based on literature-correlation analysis of reported Ni─Mn P2-type cathodes, we establish a machine-learning-guided dopant-class design strategy. The analysis reveals distinct roles of metal, non-metal, and metalloid dopants in governing cycling stability and redox reversibility, identifying metalloid regulation as the most favorable direction for enhancing high-voltage structural and redox stability. Guided by this insight, an Al─B─F co-doped P2-type cathode is rationally designed, in which boron reinforces the oxygen framework through strong B─O covalency, while Al and F provide complementary cationic and anionic regulation. The optimized cathode delivers 142.8 mAh g −1 at a high average voltage of 3.53 V and exhibits superior low-temperature capacity retention of 98.19% after 300 cycles at −5 C. In situ XRD, soft x-ray absorption spectroscopy, ex situ XPS, operando DEMS, and DFT calculations reveal a highly reversible reaction pathway featuring stabilized oxygen redox and near-zero volumetric strain (ΔV/V ≈ 0.025%). This work establishes machine-learning-guided dopant-class design as a general strategy for developing durable high-voltage layered sodium-ion cathodes.

10.1002/adfm.78581.title: Hijacking Tumor GLUT1 With a Disassemblable Self-Enhancing Nanoreactor for Metabolic Exhaustion and Anti-Angiogenesis
10.1002/adfm.78581.abstract: ABSTRACT While tumor cells exhibit a well-known dependence on glucose, effectively exploiting this vulnerability has been challenging. Achieving sustained and intensive glucose consumption and overcoming tumor metabolic adaptability as well as compensatory angiogenesis remain unsolved problems. This study developed a disassemblable, self-enhancing nanoreactor (GCG). The design centers on a positive feedback loop built upon the glucose transporter GLUT1. GCG is efficiently internalized by hijacking GLUT1, which is overexpressed on tumor cells. Once inside the tumor-specific high-glutathione (GSH) environment, it disassembles and activates glucose oxidase (GOx), leading to rapid intracellular glucose depletion. This deprived state, in turn, induces up-regulation of GLUT1 expression in tumor cells, recruiting more GCG nanoreactors and establishing a self-enhancing cycle of glucose deprivation. These results indicated that this strategy enabled rapid and sustained glucose consumption in the oxygen-rich superficial regions of tumors, thereby cutting off the nutrient supply to deeper tumor areas and successfully inducing disulfidptosis via NADPH exhaustion. Concurrently, the resulting extreme glucose scarcity effectively inhibited endothelial cell sprouting and migration, achieving synergistic anti-angiogenesis. Consequently, this self-enhancing metabolic intervention exhibited superior tumor suppression (87% inhibition) and anti-metastatic efficacy. Importantly, it presents a promising therapeutic strategy for tumor therapy by orchestrating self-enhancing glucose deprivation.

10.1002/adfm.78956.title: Fatigue-Resistant Mechanically Interlocked Co-Crosslinked Polyimide Films for Reliable High-Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
10.1002/adfm.78956.abstract: ABSTRACT During long-term operation, repeated thermal expansion and contraction inevitably generate cyclic thermal stresses that cause dielectric film buckling, cracking, and eventual device failure. As promising candidates for next-generation dielectric films, polyimides (PIs) are therefore required to combine high energy-storage performance with mechanical fatigue resistance under coupled thermal, electrical, and mechanical stresses. Here, we report a mechanically interlocked crosslinked topology designed to meet this requirement. A maleimide-functionalized crown ether monomer (CM) forms mechanically interlocked junctions with PI chains, while co-crosslinking with a bismaleimide monomer (SiMI) extends these junctions into a three-dimensional network and creates nanoscale multiphase interfaces through SiMI self-crosslinking. This topology improves high-temperature energy-storage performance and imparts strong mechanical integrity to the PI films, especially resistance to mechanical fatigue. Dielectric-optimized PI-CM0.75-M7.5 achieves a breakdown strength of 600 MV/m at 200°C and maintains η ≥ 90% up to 450 MV/m. Mechanically optimized PI-CM0.25-M2.5 shows a Young's modulus of 2.9 GPa and a stable cyclic mechanical response, with only 5.8% stress decay after 50 tensile loading-unloading cycles and a peak stress that approaches a plateau during cycling. This work provides a topology-guided strategy for balancing thermal stability, high-temperature dielectric energy storage, and cyclic mechanical reliability in polymer dielectrics.

10.1002/adfm.78982.title: Beyond Monolayers: Opportunities and Challenges in Wafer-Scale Multilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
10.1002/adfm.78982.abstract: ABSTRACT Multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), with their tunable layer numbers and stacking configurations, provide a key platform for designing electronic and optical properties beyond the monolayer limit, promising to drive the development of next-generation semiconductor technologies. However, the promise of multilayer TMDs remains limited by the lack of scalable synthesis routes that enable large-area growth with precise control over thickness, stacking sequence, and material quality. From the perspective of energy competition during the growth process, we systematically analyze four principal growth paradigms: layer-by-layer epitaxy, step-edge-guided-growth, hypotaxy (‘hypo’ meaning downward and ‘taxy’ meaning arrangement), and interfacial epitaxy, while also outlining corresponding improvement strategies for each paradigm. Looking forward, we discuss the future trajectory of the field, highlighting the viable routes to evolve from the current paradigm of imprecise kinetic control to one of atomically precise fabrication. This perspective not only furnishes tangible strategies but also provides promising directions for achieving the controlled, scalable production of large-area multilayer TMDs.

10.1002/adfm.78992.title: Enhanced Energy Storage Performance of High-Temperature Dielectric Films by Internally Constructing Oriented Microfibril Structure
10.1002/adfm.78992.abstract: ABSTRACT High-temperature dielectric films are essential components for capacitive energy storage in severe environments, ranging from hybrid electric vehicles to power systems. However, the surge in leakage current at elevated temperatures leads to a dramatic decrease in discharge energy efficiency, falling well short of the requirements for the next-generation high-temperature polymer dielectrics. Herein, a novel technology of “melting extrusion-hot stretching-quenching” was utilized to generate high-temperature polycarbonate (HTPC)-based dielectric films, where the compatible blends of polymethyl methacrylate/polyvinylidene fluoride (PMMA/PVDF) were in situ formed into highly aligned microfibrils. The well-designed microfibrils enhanced the interfacial polarization and efficiently served as carrier traps, thereby synergistically improving the discharge energy density and discharge energy efficiency at high temperature. Consequently, the as-prepared all-organic dielectric film exhibited an appreciable discharge energy density as high as 6.54 J/cm 3 with a discharge energy efficiency of 87.5% at 600 MV/m and 120°C. After being continuously charged and discharged at 300 MV/m and 120°C for 10 5 times, a negligible attenuation was observed in energy storage properties. This work provides a feasible way to tailor the comprehensive performance of HTPC by internally constructing oriented microfibril structure, thereby advancing the design and scalable fabrication of HTPC-engineered dielectric films for high-temperature energy storage.

10.1002/adfm.79015.title: Topology-Guided Hierarchical Programming of Transfer Characteristics in Single-Molecule Electrochemical Transistors
10.1002/adfm.79015.abstract: ABSTRACT Hierarchical control of molecular transport requires not only multiple regulatory inputs, but also a relationship in which an initial structural feature influences how a subsequent stimulus modifies the transport response. Here, we investigate this concept using two azulene-based molecular wires that share the same conjugated core and thioether anchor chemistry but differ in the position of one terminal anchoring group on an ancillary phenyl ring. Electrochemically gated scanning tunneling microscope break junction measurements were used to map their conductance-potential characteristics over the same potential window in both the neutral and protonated states. This matched four-state comparison reveals opposite monotonic conductance responses for the neutral para- and meta-linked junctions. Upon protonation, the para derivative develops a peak-shaped anti-ambipolar characteristic, whereas the meta derivative exhibits a valley-shaped ambipolar response. These distinct changes indicate that protonation does not modify the two junctions uniformly, but instead produces transfer characteristics that depend on the pre-existing anchoring topology. Our findings suggest that molecular topology can be used not only to tune an initial transport state, but also to shape its response to a subsequent chemical input, offering a strategy for constructing molecular junctions with differentiated gate-response functions.

10.1002/adfm.79002.title: Side-Chain Terminal Engineering Enables 18% Efficient Non-Fused Ring Electron Acceptor Organic Solar Cells via Crystallization Control
10.1002/adfm.79002.abstract: ABSTRACT Non-fused ring electron acceptors (NFREAs) provide a low-cost alternative to fused-ring electron acceptors for organic solar cells (OSCs). Nevertheless, how terminal substituents on alkyl side chains modulate the crystallization behavior of NFREAs remains largely underexplored. Herein, two NFREAs, namely TTF-F (fluorine-terminated side chains) and TTO-F (methoxy-terminated side chains), were constructed with identical intramolecular conformational locks and terminal IC acceptor units. Although the two molecules possess nearly identical electronic structures, in situ UV-vis absorption spectroscopy confirms that TTF-F exhibits much faster crystallization kinetics (completing aggregation within 206 ms) relative to TTO-F (336 ms). Femtosecond transient absorption measurements demonstrate that the hole-transfer process in D18: TTF-F blends proceeds fourfold more rapidly (τ 1 = 0.26 ps) than that in D18: TTO-F (τ 1 = 1.14 ps), consistent with the more ordered π - π stacking revealed by grazing-incidence wide-angle x-ray scattering (GIWAXS). When paired with the polymer donor D18, TTF-F delivers an outstanding power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.02%, far exceeding the 13.35% efficiency of TTO-F -based devices. This substantial performance discrepancy mainly stems from distinct crystallization dynamics and resultant thin-film microstructures. This work establishes a structure-kinetics-morphology-performance relationship for NFREAs by tuning side-chain terminal groups and offers rational molecular design strategies to fabricate high-efficiency NFREA-based OSCs.

10.1002/adfm.78954.title: Coordination-Gated MOF@COF Functional Separators for Regulating Ion Flux in Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78954.abstract: ABSTRACT Functional separators that regulate ion transport before lithium ions (Li + ) reach the lithium metal surface are critical for mitigating dendritic deposition and interfacial instability in lithium metal batteries. However, most separator designs mainly emphasize Li + affinity or electrolyte wettability, while the migration and decomposition behavior of anions remains insufficiently controlled. Herein, a coordination-gated anion-sieving separator is developed by constructing a UiO-66@F-COF@Ni core-shell interlayer on commercial polypropylene. In this architecture, the UiO-66 core provides stable porous transport channels, and the fluorinated imine-linked COF shell creates a polar ion-regulating interface. The introduced Ni 2+ coordination centers interact with PF 6 − to modulate anion migration and interfacial decomposition. Benefiting from the coupled MOF@COF heterointerface and anion-sieving effect, the separator exhibits high ionic conductivity, enhanced Li + transference, and reduced interfacial resistance. The regulated ion flux alleviates concentration polarization, guides uniform Li deposition, and promotes the formation of a compact inorganic-rich SEI. Consequently, LFP||Li batteries retain 126.1 mAh g −1 after 1200 cycles at 2.0 C, and high-voltage NCM811||Li batteries maintain 141.4 mAh g −1 after 600 cycles at 3.0 C. This coordination-regulated MOF@COF separator provides a practical strategy for stable, high-rate, and high-voltage lithium metal batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78912.title: Spatially Complementary In-Plane Lattice Strain Engineering for Reduced Contact Resistance and Enhanced Ferroelectric Switching in Van Der Waals α-In 2 Se 3 Ferroelectric Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors
10.1002/adfm.78912.abstract: ABSTRACT α-In 2 Se 3 ferroelectric semiconductor field-effect transistors (FeS-FETs) offer attractive non-volatile memory characteristics but are limited by high source/drain (S/D) contact resistance and inefficient ferroelectric polarization switching. Here, we demonstrate a low-temperature, CMOS-compatible strain-engineering strategy based on region-dependent in-plane (IP) lattice strain. A silicon nitride stress layer induces tensile strain in the S/D regions and compressive strain in the channel, producing spatially differentiated effects within a single device. The contact-side tensile strain modifies the interfacial electronic structure and reduces contact resistance, whereas the channel-side compressive strain facilitates ferroelectric polarization switching. Consequently, the strained α-In 2 Se 3 FeS-FET achieves a 12.03-fold reduction in S/D contact resistance, a 19.21-fold increase in on-state current, a 4.4%p increase in normalized memory window, and a 22.4-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric resistance switching ratio. Raman characterization and finite-element method simulations establish the region-dependent strain distribution, while interface-pinning analysis and first-principles calculations provide mechanistic support for the distinct contact- and channel-side effects. These results establish region-dependent IP lattice strain as a unified device-engineering framework for jointly controlling contact transport and ferroelectric memory functionality in vdW α-In 2 Se 3 FeS-FETs.

10.1002/adfm.78967.title: Interfacial Water-Regulated High-Entropy Intermetallic Catalysts for Selective Ethylene Glycol Upgrading and Self-Powered Hydrogen Production
10.1002/adfm.78967.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective electrochemical upgrading of ethylene glycol (EG) to glycolic acid (GA) coupled with hydrogen evolution provides a promising pathway for chemical-energy co-production, yet remains challenged by CO poisoning, excessive C-C bond cleavage, and uncontrolled oxygenated intermediates on Pt-based catalysts. This work develops a platinum-based high-entropy intermetallic catalyst (Pt 4 FeCoNiCu) anchored on phosphorus-nitrogen co-doped porous carbon (HEI-PNC) for selective EG oxidation and hydrogen evolution. The ordered intermetallic lattice creates chemically diverse atomic environments that regulate interfacial water structures and oxygenated intermediate evolution during EG oxidation, thereby suppressing CO poisoning and unwanted C─C bond cleavage. Meanwhile, electronic redistribution within the intermetallic lattice stabilizes key C2 intermediates and accelerates reaction kinetics. Consequently, HEI-PNC delivers a low onset potential of 0.304 V, a 4.4-fold enhancement in Pt mass activity compared with Pt/C and achieves a glycolate Faradaic efficiency of 98.2%. Integrated into a hybrid alkali/acid fuel cell, the catalyst enables self-powered co-production of glycolate and H 2 with stable operation over 220 h. This work highlights interfacial water-regulated high-entropy intermetallic catalysis as an effective strategy for selective polyol upgrading and chemical-energy co-production.

10.1002/adfm.78578.title: Balancing Temperature Stability and Dielectric Loss in Microwave Ceramics via Embedded Polar Nanoregions
10.1002/adfm.78578.abstract: ABSTRACT The deployment of 5G/6G communication systems demands microwave dielectric ceramics that simultaneously possess a near-zero temperature coefficient of resonant frequency and an ultra-low dielectric loss (tan δ ), which represents a long-standing challenge that demands effective optimization strategies. Herein, the fundamental limitation is substantially alleviated by a strategy integrating interpretable machine learning with entropy engineering, enabling the reverse design of a medium-entropy perovskite microwave ceramic composition (Ca 0.7 Sm 0.27 Nd 0.03 )[Ti 0.686 (Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 ) 0.014 Al 0.3 ]O 3 . This ceramic material delivers a desired combination perfomance of τ f = −0.18 ppm/°C and tan δ = 1.19 × 10 −4 at 4.6 GHz. Multiscale characterization reveals that entropy-induced chemical disorder creates isolated polar nanoregions that pin charged defects, transforming them from a source of relaxation loss into static structural units, which is different from the conventional defect-loss correlation mechanism. The optimized ceramic is implemented in a dielectric resonator antenna, which demonstrates superior performance: a radiation efficiency of 96.2% and a gain of 6.06 dBi. The findings establish a generalizable framework for navigating complex compositional spaces and resolving conflicting properties in perovskite materials.

10.1002/adfm.78933.title: Cu-Mo Plasmonic Coupling Generates Enhanced Local Electromagnetic Fields in Co 0.5 Cu 0.5 /Mo Heterostructures for Photocatalytic Ammonia Borane Hydrolysis
10.1002/adfm.78933.abstract: ABSTRACT Plasmon-mediated catalysis provides a promising route for enhancing photocatalytic hydrogen generation from ammonia borane (NH 3 BH 3 ), yet the reaction rate remains limited by insufficient charge generation and separation. Herein, we address this limitation by developing a plasmonic coupling strategy to generate enhanced local electromagnetic fields in a ternary Co 0.5 Cu 0.5 /Mo. Cu nanoparticles are dispersed on Mo and Co nanosheets are anchored on Mo and extend toward the Cu nanoparticles. Co 0.5 Cu 0.5 /Mo catalyst achieves an outstanding turnover frequency of 162.8 min −1 under steady-state H 2 flow for photocatalytic NH 3 BH 3 hydrolysis at 298 K, outperforming Co/Mo and Cu/Mo by factors of approximately 1.5 and 5.0, respectively, and surpassing most reported noble-metal-free catalysts under comparable conditions. Combined spectroscopic characterizations, surface enhanced Raman scattering, in situ x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations reveal that the synergistic plasmonic coupling between Mo with a partially oxidized surface and Cu intensifies the local electromagnetic field, promotes charge generation and separation, and induces preferential electron accumulation on Cu. This redistribution enlarges the electron density difference between Cu and Co active sites, thereby facilitating the activation of NH 3 BH 3 and H 2 O and accelerating hydrogen evolution. This study provides a feasible strategy for engineering electromagnetic-field-enhanced non-precious-metal catalysts for NH 3 BH 3 hydrolysis and related hydrogen-generation reactions.

10.1002/adfm.78853.title: Record-High Birefringence Achieved by Linearly Extended π-Conjugated Building Blocks in Metal-Free Sulfate
10.1002/adfm.78853.abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of birefringent materials is critical for next-generation integrated photonics, yet conventional systems face intrinsic limitations in birefringence magnitude. Sulfate crystals offer a promising platform but have been hindered by their dependence on specific metal cations and insufficient optical anisotropy. Here, we report a molecular design strategy that overcomes these constraints by employing linearly extended π-conjugated organic cations as high-anisotropy building units. Through rational amino-functionalization of C 12 H 8 N 2 , we engineer the novel cation [H 2 (C 12 H 10 N 4 )] 2 + , which exhibits an exceptional polarizability anisotropy of 156.7 a.u. Using a mild aqueous route, a metal-free sulfate crystal, [H 2 (C 12 H 10 N 4 )]SO 4 ·3H 2 O was synthesized, which achieves a record birefringence of 0.981 at 550 nm, surpassing all known sulfate birefringent materials and outperforming commercial benchmarks and setting a new performance standard for birefringent sulfates. Structural analysis reveals that the cations align via hydrogen-bond-directed assembly with sulfate tetrahedra into a quasi-two-dimensional anisotropic structure, thereby maximizing the macroscopic optical response. This study demonstrates that incorporating linearly extended π-conjugated organic building blocks into sulfate frameworks sever as a robust strategy for discovering highly birefringent crystals.

10.1002/adfm.78700.title: Ultrafast Magneto-Geometric Control of Terahertz Helicity in Curved Ni Metasurfaces
10.1002/adfm.78700.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic helicity control in the terahertz (THz) regime is essential for ultrafast polarization optics, chiral spectroscopy, and polarization-selective photonic devices, yet remains difficult because most THz chiral systems are structurally fixed or rely on slow external tuning. To address this, we report a curved Ni split-ring metasurface enabling magnetically amplified and ultrafast reconfigurable THz helicity control. Handed curvature breaks mirror symmetry and produces opposite static circular dichroism in left-handed and right-handed metasurfaces, accompanied by a near order-of-magnitude increase in current asymmetry compared to flat and achiral references. In pump-free steady-state THz transmission, in-plane magnetization increases the static CD contrast from 9.4 to 33.6 (3.57-fold enhancement). In optical pump-THz probe measurements, magnetization further increases the normalized transient circular dichroism contrast from 0.538 to 1.553 (2.89-fold enhancement). The magnetized response exhibits switching-like TRCD reweighting within τ ≈ 0.5 ps, consistent with ultrafast transient helicity control. These results show that femtosecond excitation reweights a pre-existing magneto-geometric chiral state rather than creating an independent photoinduced chiral structure. This work provides a lithography-compatible route to ultrafast, reversible, and magnetically enhanced THz helicity control.

10.1002/adfm.78991.title: Leaf-Inspired Biomimetic Porous Hydrogels for Multi-Band Camouflage
10.1002/adfm.78991.abstract: ABSTRACT With the development of visible, hyperspectral, and thermal-infrared multi-band reconnaissance technologies, achieving an ideal camouflage in the jungle environment remains a major challenge. Inspired by green leaves, this work designs and prepares a flame-retardant and robust biomimetic porous hydrogel (BPH), which not only mimics the color and visible-near-infrared reflectance spectral characteristics of natural leaves, but also simulates the moisture absorption-transpiration behavior for thermal management. The color difference between BPH and leaf is only 1.87, making them barely distinguishable by naked eyes. Importantly, BPH exhibits a visible-near infrared reflectance spectrum similar to that of natural leaf, with the spectral correlation coefficient and cosine similarity as high as 0.940 and 0.958, respectively. In addition, the radiative temperature difference between BPH and surrounding leaves does not exceed 2°C. Furthermore, BPH could serve as a coating to endow conventional fabrics with superior visible, hyperspectral, and thermal infrared camouflage performance in outdoor jungle environments, thereby acting as camouflage barriers such as tents and camouflage nets. This work provides a novel strategy for the design and preparation of visible, hyperspectral, and thermal infrared camouflage materials, aiming to address the challenge of multi-band camouflage compatibility and enhance the battlefield survivability of targets.

10.1002/adfm.78979.title: Magnetically Reconfigurable Noncollinear Excitonic Polarization in a MoSe 2 /CrOCl/Fe 3 GaTe 2 Heterostructure
10.1002/adfm.78979.abstract: ABSTRACT Van der Waals (vdW) heterointerfaces provide a versatile platform for tailoring polarization-resolved excitonic emission in 2D semiconductors, offering new opportunities for polarization-encoded photonic functionalities. However, the realization of distinct and externally reconfigurable polarization orientations for coexisting excitonic states within a single magnetic heterostructure remains largely unexplored. Here we demonstrate magnetically reconfigurable exciton polarization in a MoSe 2 /CrOCl/Fe 3 GaTe 2 vdW heterostructure, arising from the combined effects of interfacial symmetry breaking and magnetically mediated interfacial coupling. Polarization-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal pronounced in-plane anisotropy for both neutral excitons (X 0 ) and trions (T), with strongly non-collinear polarization axes. Near the spin-flop transition of CrOCl, the emission polarization undergoes an abrupt ∼ 90°rotation under an applied magnetic field, generating bistable polarization states that allow optical readout of magnetic phase evolution and dual-channel polarization encoding. A further reorientation across the Néel temperature highlights the intimate coupling between magnetic order and lattice symmetry at the heterointerface. First-principles calculations attribute the emergent anisotropy to anisotropic charge redistribution in MoSe 2 . These findings establish magnetic vdW heterointerfaces as a route to reconfigurable multi-exciton polarization control and magnetic-field-tunable polarization encoding in 2D materials.

10.1002/adfm.78953.title: A High-Performance Flexible All-Solid-State Supercapacitor Integrating 3D Interpenetrating MXene/GNS@CC Electrodes and a Self-Healing Hydrogel Electrolyte
10.1002/adfm.78953.abstract: ABSTRACT This work presents a flexible, self-healing supercapacitor (SHSC) comprising an MXene/graphene nanoscrolls@carbon cloth (MXene/GNS@CC) composite electrode and a self-healing poly(vinyl alcohol)-polydopamine (PVA-PDA) hydrogel electrolyte. The MXene/GNS@CC electrode was directly fabricated on carbon cloth through a one-step electrophoretic deposition (EPD) strategy, in which graphene nanoscrolls (GNS) were interwoven among the MXene nanosheets to construct a three-dimensional (3D) interpenetrating architecture. This architecture suppressed nanosheet restacking, increased accessible surface area, facilitated ion transport, and improved mechanical reliability. The resulting electrode was further integrated with a self-healingPVA-PDA hydrogel electrolyte to assemble an all-in-one supercapacitor. Owing to the abundant catechol groups in PDA, the hydrogel electrolyte exhibited excellent self-healing capability and strong interfacial adhesion. Moreover, hydrogen-bonding interactions with the terminal groups on the MXene surface and π - π conjugation interactions with GNS contributed to the formation of a robust 3D network. Consequently, the MXene/GNS@CC electrode delivered an areal capacitance of 6880.60 mF·cm −2 at 1 mA·cm −2 . The assembled SHSC achieved an areal capacitance of 1152.03 mF·cm −2 at 1 mA·cm −2 and an areal energy density of 195.37 µWh·cm −2 at a power density of 0.61 mW·cm −2 . Additionally, the device retained 87.32% of its initial capacitance even after four cutting/healing cycles, indicating its broad application prospects in the field of flexible self-healing energy-storage devices.

10.1002/adfm.78983.title: Reprogramming Sphingolipid Metabolic and Redox Homeostasis with an Injectable Botanicals/Nanozymes Hydrogel for Inhibiting Postoperative Recurrence and Metastasis in Breast Cancer
10.1002/adfm.78983.abstract: ABSTRACT Postoperative recurrence and metastasis in breast cancer remain major clinical challenges, primarily driven by persistent inflammation responses and secondary infections at surgical sites.
